properties.label: Out of Taiwan
properties.summary: Austronesian-speaking farmers and voyagers spread from Taiwan through the Philippines towards the Moluccas, ancestors of the Lapita people.

properties.label: Marianas
properties.summary: First long open-sea crossing in human history, from the Philippines some 2,300 km to Guam and Saipan.

properties.label: Aegean Bronze Age
properties.summary: Starting world c. 1400 BC: the Aegean coasts and islands, Crete, Rhodes and western Anatolia, with contacts to Cyprus, the Levant coast, the Nile delta and Amarna, and Mycenaean trade points in southern Italy, the Aeolian islands and eastern Sicily.

properties.leader: Lapita culture in the Bismarck Archipelago
properties.label: Lapita: Bismarcks
properties.summary: The Lapita cultural complex, with its dentate-stamped pottery, appears in the Bismarck Archipelago (Mussau, New Britain, New Ireland).

properties.label: Lapita: New Caledonia
properties.summary: Lapita voyagers settled the Loyalty Islands and Grande Terre, naming the type site at Lapita (Kone).

properties.label: Zhou China
properties.summary: The Yellow River heartland of the Shang and Western Zhou: the Wei valley, the central plain, Shandong and Yan.

properties.leader: Lapita crossing into Remote Oceania (Reef and Santa Cruz)
properties.label: Lapita: Santa Cruz
properties.summary: Lapita voyagers passed the inhabited main Solomons to settle the Reef and Santa Cruz Islands, the first step into Remote Oceania.

properties.label: Lapita: Vanuatu
properties.summary: First settlement of Vanuatu, including the Teouma cemetery on Efate.

properties.label: Lapita: Fiji
properties.summary: Settlement of Fiji from Vanuatu, the gateway to Polynesia; earliest site at Bourewa on Viti Levu.

properties.label: Lapita: Tonga
properties.summary: First settlement of Tonga at Nukuleka on Tongatapu, the earliest site in Polynesia.

properties.leader: Lapita settlement of Wallis, Futuna and Samoa
properties.label: Lapita: Samoa
properties.summary: Lapita settlers reached Futuna, Uvea and Samoa (Mulifanua), completing the settlement of West Polynesia.

properties.label: Kition
properties.summary: Phoenician settlement at Kition on Cyprus, the first step of Tyre's westward expansion.

properties.label: Carthage founded
properties.summary: Tyrians found Carthage on the Gulf of Tunis, opening the central Mediterranean sea route west.

properties.label: Gadir
properties.summary: Tyrian foundation of Gadir (Cadiz) beyond the Pillars of Heracles, the Phoenician gateway to the Atlantic and the silver of Tartessos.

properties.label: Sardinia
properties.summary: Phoenician settlements at Caralis, Nora, Sulcis and Tharros along the southern and western coasts of Sardinia.

properties.label: Utica
properties.summary: Phoenician colony of Utica on the Tunisian coast.

properties.leader: Euboean colonists of Chalcis and Eretria
properties.label: Pithekoussai
properties.summary: Euboean Greeks settle Pithekoussai (Ischia) and Cumae, the first Greek colonies in Italy.

properties.label: Homeric world
properties.summary: Starting world c. 750 BC: the Aegean, the Hellespont and the entrance to the Black Sea, Sicily and southern Italy, Egypt and the Nile up to Thebes, Phoenicia (Sidon), Cyprus and the Libyan coast, as reflected in the Homeric poems and the first Euboean colonies.

properties.label: Lixus
properties.summary: Phoenician colony at Lixus on the Loukkos estuary, first foothold on Africa's Atlantic coast.

properties.label: W Sicily and Malta
properties.summary: Phoenician settlements on Malta and at Motya, Panormus (Palermo) and Solus in western Sicily.

properties.label: Greek Sicily
properties.summary: Greek colonies ring eastern and southern Sicily: Naxos, Syracuse, Gela, Akragas and Selinus.

properties.label: Magna Graecia
properties.summary: Achaean and Spartan colonies at Sybaris, Croton and Taras round the Gulf of Taranto.

properties.label: Byzantium
properties.summary: Megarians found Byzantium and Chalcedon at the Bosporus, the gateway to the Black Sea.

properties.label: Ibiza
properties.summary: Settlement of Ebusus (Ibiza) in the Balearics, described as Carthage's first recorded independent action.

properties.label: Mogador
properties.summary: Phoenician trading station on Mogador Island (Essaouira), the southernmost known Phoenician site on the Atlantic.

properties.label: Colaeus to Tartessos
properties.summary: A Samian trader driven west beyond the Pillars of Heracles reaches Tartessos, the first recorded Greek visit to Atlantic Spain.

properties.label: Cyrene
properties.summary: Therans under Battus found Cyrene (inland of its port Apollonia), opening Greek knowledge of Libya.

properties.label: Istros and Olbia
properties.summary: Milesian colonies on the western and northern Black Sea: Apollonia, Istros, Tyras, Berezan and Olbia at the Dnieper-Bug estuary.

properties.label: Sinope
properties.summary: Milesians found Sinope on the southern Black Sea coast, base for Pontic expansion.

properties.label: Naucratis
properties.summary: Greek trading post of Naucratis on the Canopic Nile, Greece's window on Egypt.

properties.leader: Spring and Autumn states of the Yangtze (base)
properties.label: Chu, Wu, Yue
properties.summary: The middle and lower Yangtze states of Chu, Wu and Yue as they entered the Chinese record.

properties.label: Panticapaeum
properties.summary: Greek colonies in Crimea and the Kerch strait (Panticapaeum, Theodosia, Phanagoria), later the Bosporan kingdom.

properties.leader: Phoenician crews of Pharaoh Necho II
properties.label: Circumnavigation of Africa
properties.summary: Herodotus reports Phoenicians sent by Necho II sailed from the Red Sea round Libya (Africa) and back through the Pillars in three years.

properties.label: Massalia
properties.summary: Phocaeans found Massalia (Marseille) near the Rhone mouth, with Alalia on Corsica and later Elea.

properties.label: Trapezus and Phasis
properties.summary: Colonies along the eastern Black Sea at Amisos, Trapezus, Phasis in Colchis and Dioscurias.

properties.label: Emporion and Tartessos
properties.summary: Phocaeans found Emporion and trade down the Iberian coast to Tartessos, whose king Arganthonios befriended them.

properties.label: Euthymenes
properties.summary: A Massaliote voyage down Africa's Atlantic coast to a great crocodile-filled river, probably the Senegal.

properties.label: Scylax down the Indus
properties.summary: A Carian Greek in Persian service sails down the Indus to the sea, the first Greek account of India.

properties.label: Scylax round Arabia
properties.summary: Scylax sails west from the Indus mouth and round Arabia to Suez, 30 months in all.

properties.label: Hecataeus' map
properties.summary: World of Hecataeus' Periodos Ges c. 500 BC: a coastal circuit from the Pillars of Heracles clockwise round the Mediterranean and Black Sea to Atlantic Morocco, with Egypt and the Persian heartland along the Royal Road.

properties.label: Hanno
properties.summary: Carthaginian fleet of 60 ships founds colonies on Atlantic Morocco and sails down West Africa past the Senegal toward a burning mountain and the 'Gorillai'.

properties.label: Himilco
properties.summary: Carthaginian voyage north along Atlantic Iberia to the tin lands of the Oestrymnides (Brittany), perhaps the British Isles.

properties.label: Herodotus in Egypt
properties.summary: Herodotus travels up the Nile to Elephantine and records Egypt and hearsay of Meroe and Nubia beyond.

properties.label: Herodotus in Asia
properties.summary: Herodotus' travels in Syria and Mesopotamia, possibly to Babylon and Susa, describing the Persian empire.

properties.label: Herodotus in Scythia
properties.summary: Herodotus visits the Black Sea and the Scythian coast to the Borysthenes (Dnieper), gathering the first detailed account of the steppe peoples.

properties.leader: Cyrus the Younger and the Ten Thousand (Xenophon)
properties.label: Anabasis: march up
properties.summary: The march of the Ten Thousand from Sardis through Cilicia and down the Euphrates to Cunaxa near Babylon.

properties.label: Anabasis: retreat
properties.summary: Retreat of the Ten Thousand up the Tigris, through the Carduchian mountains and Armenian winter to the Black Sea at Trapezus.

properties.label: Anabasis: coast
properties.summary: The Ten Thousand move west along the Pontic coast by ship and on foot via Cotyora, Sinope and Heraclea to Byzantium.

properties.label: Alexander: Danube
properties.summary: Alexander's Balkan campaign across the Haemus to the Danube and into Illyria.

properties.label: Alexander: Asia Minor to Egypt
properties.summary: Alexander crosses to Asia, wins at the Granicus and Issus, takes Tyre and Gaza and enters Egypt, founding Alexandria and visiting Siwa.

properties.label: Alexander: Mesopotamia and Persia
properties.summary: Alexander marches across Mesopotamia to Gaugamela, takes Babylon, Susa and Persepolis, then Ecbatana.

properties.label: Alexander: Iran to Central Asia
properties.summary: Pursuit of Darius and Bessus through Parthia, Aria, Drangiana and Arachosia, over the Hindu Kush to Bactria and Sogdiana as far as the Jaxartes.

properties.label: Alexander: into India
properties.summary: Alexander crosses the Hindu Kush into the Kabul valley and Swat, crosses the Indus, defeats Porus on the Hydaspes and reaches the Hyphasis (Beas).

properties.label: Alexander: down the Indus
properties.summary: Fleet and army descend the Hydaspes, Acesines and Indus to Patala and the Indus delta.

properties.label: Alexander: Gedrosia
properties.summary: Return through the Gedrosian desert (Makran) and Carmania to Persepolis, Susa, Opis and Babylon.

properties.label: Craterus via Arachosia
properties.summary: Craterus leads the heavy troops and elephants from the Indus through the Bolan pass, Arachosia and Drangiana to Carmania.

properties.label: Nearchus
properties.summary: Nearchus sails the fleet from the Indus along the Makran coast and up the Persian Gulf to the Tigris mouth, charting the route by sea.

properties.label: Pytheas: Britain and Thule
properties.summary: Pytheas sails from Massalia out of the Mediterranean, round Brittany and Britain and north to Thule, giving the first account of the British Isles and the Arctic north.

properties.label: Pytheas: amber coast
properties.summary: Pytheas visits the amber coast of northern Europe (Abalus) and the Guiones, perhaps turning back at the Vistula.

properties.label: Megasthenes
properties.summary: Seleucid envoy Megasthenes travels from Arachosia through the Punjab and down the Ganges plain to Pataliputra, writing the Indica.

properties.label: Patrocles on the Caspian
properties.summary: Seleucid admiral Patrocles explores the Caspian Sea, wrongly concluding it was a gulf of the outer Ocean.

properties.label: Tanais
properties.summary: Bosporan Greek trading city of Tanais at the mouth of the Don, the edge of the Greek world toward the steppe.

properties.label: Cisalpine Gaul
properties.summary: Rome conquers the Po valley after Telamon, founding Placentia, Cremona, Bononia and Aquileia.

properties.label: Qin empire
properties.summary: The unified Qin empire with Sichuan, Lingnan, Liaodong and the Ordos frontier of the Great Wall.

properties.leader: Gnaeus and Publius Cornelius Scipio, Scipio Africanus
properties.label: Scipios in Spain
properties.summary: Roman armies land at Emporion and fight Carthage down eastern and southern Spain to Carthago Nova, Baecula, Ilipa and Gades.

properties.label: Cato in Spain
properties.summary: Cato subdues Hispania Citerior north of the Ebro, marches into Turdetania and the Celtiberian interior at Segestica (Siguenza).

properties.label: Gracchus in Celtiberia
properties.summary: Gracchus campaigns in the Ebro valley and Celtiberian plateau, founding Gracchurris and making treaties with the Celtiberians.

properties.label: Lucullus in the Meseta
properties.summary: Lucullus pushes west across the Duero plateau against the Vaccaei at Cauca, Intercatia and Pallantia, with Scipio Aemilianus serving under him.

properties.label: Polybius' Atlantic voyage
properties.summary: After the fall of Carthage, Polybius explores Africa's Atlantic coast with a fleet lent by Scipio Aemilianus.

properties.label: Zhang Qian
properties.summary: First Chinese envoy to the west: reached Dayuan (Ferghana), Kangju, the Yuezhi and Daxia (Bactria), and reported on Parthia and India.

properties.label: Hexi Corridor
properties.summary: Han armies took the Hexi Corridor from the Xiongnu and founded the four commanderies to Dunhuang and the Jade Gate.

properties.label: Zhang Qian: Wusun
properties.summary: Embassy to the Wusun of the Ili and Issyk Kul region; his deputies went on to Dayuan, Kangju, the Yuezhi, Daxia, Anxi (Parthia) and Shendu.

properties.label: Eudoxus to India
properties.summary: Eudoxus, guided by a shipwrecked Indian sailor, sails from Egypt to India and back, and on a second voyage is blown down the Somali coast.

properties.label: Eudoxus
properties.summary: First Greek voyage on the monsoon route straight across the Arabian Sea from the Red Sea to India.

properties.label: Nanyue, Jiaozhi
properties.summary: Conquest of Nanyue added Lingnan, Hainan and the Red River delta, with Rinan commandery reaching central Vietnam.

properties.label: Eudoxus (Atlantic)
properties.summary: Attempt to sail from Gades round Africa down the Atlantic coast of Morocco; turned back, a later attempt vanished.

properties.label: Lelang
properties.summary: Han armies took Wanggeom (Pyongyang) and set up the Four Commanderies including Lelang in north Korea.

properties.leader: Li Guangli (War of the Heavenly Horses)
properties.label: Ferghana war
properties.summary: Han army crossed the Tarim and the Tian Shan to besiege Ershi, capital of Dayuan in the Ferghana valley.

properties.leader: Han envoys to Huangzhi (Book of Han)
properties.label: Han sea route to India
properties.summary: Book of Han itinerary from Rinan and Hepu along Indochina to Dulu and Huangzhi (probably Kanchipuram) and Yichengbu (Sri Lanka).

properties.label: Pompey
properties.summary: Roman army pursuing Mithridates crossed Armenia into Iberia and Albania (Georgia, Azerbaijan) and reached the Phasis, bringing the Caucasus into Roman knowledge.

properties.label: Caesar in Gaul
properties.summary: Caesar's eight-year conquest mapped all of Gaul from the Alps to the Channel and the Rhine, with first-hand descriptions of Gaulish and German peoples.

properties.label: Caesar to Britain
properties.summary: First Roman crossing to Britain, landing on the Kent coast between Hythe and Sandwich.

properties.label: Caesar in Britain
properties.summary: Second invasion pushed inland across the Stour and the Thames to Cassivellaunus' stronghold, giving Rome its first description of inland Britain.

properties.label: Hippalus
properties.summary: Credited with the direct open-sea crossing to south India on the south-west monsoon, making Muziris a regular Roman port.

properties.label: Aelius Gallus
properties.summary: Roman army landed at Leuke Kome and marched six months down western Arabia to besiege Marib, bringing back the first Roman eyewitness geography of Arabia Felix.

properties.label: Petronius
properties.summary: Punitive campaign up the Nile through Lower Nubia to Napata, the Kushite royal city, after Kushite raids on Syene.

properties.label: Balbus
properties.summary: Campaign into the Fezzan that captured fifteen Garamantian settlements, the first Roman army deep in the Sahara.

properties.label: Juba II
properties.summary: Juba II's expedition to the Fortunate Isles (Canary Islands), reported by Pliny, put the Canaries on the Roman map.

properties.label: Drusus fleet
properties.summary: First Roman fleet in the North Sea: down the Rhine and the Fossa Drusiana through Lake Flevo to the Frisian coast and the land of the Chauci.

properties.label: Drusus to the Elbe
properties.summary: Drusus marched from the Lippe to the Weser (11 BC) and from Mainz through the Chatti and Cherusci to the Elbe (9 BC), the furthest east any Roman army had gone in Germany.

properties.label: Parthian Stations
properties.summary: Greek itinerary of caravan stations across the Parthian empire, from the Euphrates to Arachosia (Kandahar), possibly written for Augustus' grandson Gaius Caesar.

properties.label: Fleet round Jutland
properties.summary: The Roman fleet sailed past the Elbe mouth up the coast of Jutland to the land of the Cimbri and the Skaw, glimpsing the Kattegat and the Baltic beyond.

properties.label: Tiberius to the Elbe
properties.summary: Tiberius' army marched through the Chauci and Langobardi to the lower Elbe, where it met the fleet.

properties.label: Germanicus
properties.summary: Germanicus moved his army by a fleet of about a thousand ships from the Rhine through Lake Flevo to the Ems before marching to the Weser; the fleet was wrecked by a North Sea storm on return.

properties.label: Suetonius over the Atlas
properties.summary: First Roman army to cross the Atlas mountains, reaching the desert river Ger beyond; Pliny quotes his description.

properties.label: Periplus: Africa
properties.summary: Greek merchant's handbook describing every port down the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa to Rhapta on the Tanzanian coast, the furthest south Roman knowledge reached.

properties.label: Periplus: Arabia & India
properties.summary: The Periplus describes the incense coast of Arabia, the Indus port of Barbarikon, Barygaza, the Malabar pepper ports of Muziris and Nelcynda, Roman-traded Poduke (Arikamedu) and the Ganges mouth.

properties.leader: Roman knight sent by Julianus (Nero's games)
properties.label: Amber road
properties.summary: A Roman eques travelled from Carnuntum along the Amber Road to the Baltic coast to buy amber, as Pliny reports.

properties.label: Nero's Nile party
properties.summary: Party sent by Nero up the Nile past Meroe and up the White Nile to the impassable swamps of the Sudd.

properties.label: Ban Chao
properties.summary: Thirty years restoring Han power over the Tarim kingdoms, from Shanshan and Khotan to Kashgar, Kucha and Karashahr.

properties.label: Agricola
properties.summary: Agricola's campaigns carried Roman armies through northern Britain beyond the Forth and Tay to the battle of Mons Graupius in north-east Scotland.

properties.label: Fleet round Britain
properties.summary: Agricola's fleet sailed round the north of Britain, proving it an island, subdued the Orkneys and sighted Thule (probably Shetland).

properties.label: Septimius Flaccus
properties.summary: Roman commander who marched from Garama three months south into the land of the 'Ethiopians', as reported by Marinus of Tyre via Ptolemy.

properties.label: Julius Maternus
properties.summary: Roman traveller who accompanied the Garamantian king four months south from Garama to Agisymba, a land of rhinoceroses, probably near Lake Chad.

properties.label: Gan Ying
properties.summary: Sent to reach Da Qin (Rome), he crossed Parthia to the sea at Tiaozhi (probably the head of the Persian Gulf) and turned back.

properties.label: Maes Titianus
properties.summary: Agents of the Macedonian merchant Maes Titianus travelled the Silk Road from the Euphrates through Parthia and Bactria to the Stone Tower and on to Sera, the silk capital; their distances reached Ptolemy via Marinus of Tyre.

properties.label: Trajan to the Gulf
properties.summary: Trajan's Parthian war took a Roman army down the Tigris past Ctesiphon to Charax Spasinou and the Persian Gulf.

properties.label: Ptolemy's world
properties.summary: Ptolemy's Geography (c. 150) gave coordinates for some 8,000 places from Ireland and the Canaries to the Silk Road, India, Sri Lanka and the Golden Chersonese, summing up Roman knowledge.

properties.leader: Embassy of 'Andun' (Marcus Aurelius) to Han China
properties.label: Roman embassy 166 (sea)
properties.summary: Men claiming to come from the Roman emperor 'Andun' (Antoninus) reached China by sea through Rinan in central Vietnam, the first recorded direct Roman contact with China.

properties.leader: Embassy of 'Andun' (Marcus Aurelius) to Han China
properties.label: Roman embassy 166 (land)
properties.summary: Overland stage of the 166 embassy from Rinan through Jiaozhi to the Han court at Luoyang, where it presented ivory, rhinoceros horn and tortoiseshell to Emperor Huan.

properties.leader: Wei envoys to the Wa (Weizhi Wajinden)
properties.label: Wei envoys to Wa
properties.summary: Embassies between Daifang and Queen Himiko of Yamatai, giving the first Chinese itinerary to Tsushima, Iki and Kyushu.

properties.label: Kang Tai to Funan
properties.summary: Wu envoys to Funan in the Mekong delta, whose reports described Funan and lands as far as India.

properties.label: Egeria
properties.summary: Pilgrim Egeria's letters describe Sinai, the Holy Land, Mount Nebo, Edessa and Harran in detail for readers in the far west of Europe.

properties.label: Faxian: overland
properties.summary: Overland across the Taklamakan and the Pamirs to Gandhara and the Buddhist holy places of the Ganges, the first full Chinese account of India.

properties.label: Faxian: by sea
properties.summary: From Tamralipti to Sri Lanka (two years), then via Yepoti (Java or Sumatra) home to the Shandong coast at Laoshan.

properties.label: Madagascar
properties.summary: Voyagers from southeast Borneo (Ma'anyan-related) settled Madagascar across the Indian Ocean, mixing with East Africans.

properties.leader: St Brendan of Clonfert (Navigatio Sancti Brendani)
properties.label: St Brendan (legend)
properties.summary: Legendary voyage of St Brendan to islands in the northern Ocean (perhaps the Hebrides, Faroes and Iceland), written down c. 900 and widely read in medieval Europe.

properties.label: Cosmas
properties.summary: Alexandrian merchant whose Christian Topography (c. 550) describes Adulis, Aksum, Socotra, the pepper coast of Male and Taprobane (Sri Lanka) as a hub of Indian Ocean trade.

properties.label: Zemarchus
properties.summary: Byzantine envoy who travelled to the court of the Turkic khagan Istemi in the Tian Shan, and whose report described the steppe route north of the Caspian.

properties.leader: Arabia at the rise of Islam (base)
properties.label: Arabia
properties.summary: The Arabian peninsula, its Red Sea and Gulf coasts and caravan towns, the home world of the first Muslim community.

properties.label: Xuanzang: outbound
properties.summary: Slipped out of Tang China, crossed the Tian Shan to the Western Turkic khagan at Suyab, then Samarkand, Balkh, Bamiyan and Gandhara to Kashmir.

properties.label: Xuanzang: India circuit
properties.summary: Studied at Nalanda and travelled around India from Bengal and Kamarupa to Kanchipuram, the Deccan, Gujarat and Sind.

properties.leader: Rashidun conquests of Syria, Iraq and Egypt (base)
properties.label: Syria, Iraq, Egypt
properties.summary: Syria, Palestine, Mesopotamia and Egypt as conquered by the Rashidun armies between 634 and 642.

properties.label: Wang Xuance
properties.summary: Tang envoy to King Harsha who used the new Tibet and Nepal road; in 648 he led Tibetan and Nepalese troops into north India.

properties.label: Xuanzang: return
properties.summary: Home over the Hindu Kush, Badakhshan, the Wakhan and the Pamirs to Kashgar and Khotan, reaching Chang'an in 645.

properties.label: Iran
properties.summary: The former Sasanian lands of Iran, Khurasan and the Caucasus brought into the caliphate by 651.

properties.label: Yijing
properties.summary: Sailed from Guangzhou to Srivijaya (Palembang), Malayu and Kedah and across the Bay of Bengal to Tamralipti, recording the maritime Buddhist world.

properties.label: Maghreb
properties.summary: Ifriqiya and the Maghreb to the Atlantic, conquered between the fall of Carthage (698) and about 710.

properties.label: Irish monks to the Faroes
properties.summary: Irish hermits settled the Faroe Islands about a century before the Norse, as Dicuil records.

properties.label: al-Andalus
properties.summary: Most of the Iberian peninsula and Septimania (Narbonne, 719 to 759) under Umayyad rule.

properties.label: Transoxiana, Sind
properties.summary: Transoxiana (Bukhara, Samarkand, Ferghana) taken by Qutayba ibn Muslim and Sind to Multan by Muhammad ibn Qasim, 705 to 715.

properties.label: Gao Xianzhi: Pamirs
properties.summary: Led a Tang army over the Pamirs and the Darkot pass to Little Balur (Gilgit) in 747, then west to defeat at Talas in 751.

properties.label: Du Huan
properties.summary: Captured at Talas, he lived in the Abbasid world and his Jingxingji gave the first Chinese eyewitness description of the Arabs at Kufa.

properties.leader: Jia Dan (route from Guangzhou to the Arab lands)
properties.label: Jia Dan sea route
properties.summary: Tang geographer Jia Dan's itinerary of the sea route from Guangzhou through the Strait of Malacca, Sri Lanka and India to the Euphrates mouth and Baghdad.

properties.label: Papar to Iceland
properties.summary: Irish clerics lived in Thule (Iceland) from February to August 795 and sailed a day north to the frozen sea; Dicuil wrote it down in 825.

properties.label: Charlemagne's embassy
properties.summary: Charlemagne's embassy to Harun al-Rashid in Baghdad; the sole survivor Isaac returned via Ifriqiya with the elephant Abul-Abbas.

properties.leader: Varangian Rus' (route from the Varangians to the Greeks)
properties.label: Varangians to Byzantium
properties.summary: Norse traders and warriors opened the river road from the Baltic by the Neva, Lake Ladoga, Novgorod and the Dnieper rapids to the Black Sea and Constantinople, attacked in 860.

properties.label: Sulaiman the Merchant
properties.summary: First surviving Arabic account of the sea route from Siraf via Kulam Mali, the Nicobars, Kalah and Champa to Khanfu (Guangzhou).

properties.label: Gardar
properties.summary: Gardar sailed right round Iceland, proving it an island, and wintered at Husavik.

properties.label: Naddodd
properties.summary: Norse sailor blown off course to the Faroes who reached east Iceland and named it Snaeland.

properties.label: Floki
properties.summary: Floki followed his ravens to Iceland, wintered at Vatnsfjordur in the Westfjords and gave the island its name.

properties.leader: Ibn Khordadbeh (Book of Roads and Kingdoms)
properties.label: Ibn Khordadbeh: Khurasan road
properties.summary: The Abbasid post road from Baghdad through Khurasan to Transoxiana and the Turkic steppe, with stages and distances.

properties.leader: Ibn Khordadbeh (sea route to China and al-Sila)
properties.label: Ibn Khordadbeh: al-Sila
properties.summary: First Arabic mention of al-Sila (Silla, Korea) at the far end of the sea route along the China coast.

properties.label: Radhanites
properties.summary: The northern Radhanite trade route from the land of the Franks through the Slav lands and Khazar Itil to Transoxiana and China.

properties.label: Wulfstan
properties.summary: Seven days' sail from Hedeby to Truso at the Vistula mouth, describing the Wendish coast, the Danish and Swedish islands and the Aestii, recorded for King Alfred.

properties.label: al-Ya'qubi: Kanem
properties.summary: Earliest Arabic account of the Fezzan route from Zawila to Kanem near Lake Chad, also naming Kawkaw (Gao) and Ghana.

properties.label: Ohthere to the White Sea
properties.summary: Ohthere sailed round the North Cape and along the Kola coast into the White Sea to the land of the Beormas, the first known account of the European Arctic coast.

properties.label: Ohthere to Hedeby
properties.summary: Ohthere's month-long voyage down the Norwegian coast to the market at Skiringssal (Kaupang) and on to Hedeby, the first description of Norway as a long coastal land.

properties.label: Gunnbjorn's skerries
properties.summary: Storm-driven Norse sailor who sighted islands (Gunnbjarnarsker) off east Greenland, the first European sighting of Greenland.

properties.label: Rus' to the Caspian
properties.summary: Rus' fleets reached the Caspian Sea by the Volga (and the Don portage) and raided its coasts from Baku to Abaskun and Gorgan.

properties.label: al-Mas'udi: India
properties.summary: Voyage to Sind (Mansura, Multan), Cambay, Saymur and Ceylon described in Muruj al-Dhahab.

properties.label: al-Mas'udi: Zanj
properties.summary: Sailed from Oman down the Somali and Zanj coast to Qanbalu (probably Pemba), the earliest firsthand Arabic account of the Swahili coast.

properties.leader: Swahili coast trade to Sofala (Arabic accounts)
properties.label: Swahili coast to Sofala
properties.summary: The gold and ivory trade of the Swahili towns (Zanzibar, Kilwa) reaching south to Sofala of the Zanj, as reported by al-Mas'udi.

properties.label: Ibn Fadlan
properties.summary: Embassy from Baghdad via Bukhara and Khwarazm across the Oghuz steppe to the Volga Bulgars, with the famous description of the Rus.

properties.label: Ibn Hawqal
properties.summary: Thirty years of travel (943 to 973) from Iraq across North Africa to al-Andalus and Sijilmasa, extending Arabic description to the Sahara edge.

properties.label: Rus' at Barda
properties.summary: Rus' fleet sailed down the west Caspian coast and up the Kura river to seize Barda, the capital of Arran.

properties.label: al-Muqaddasi
properties.summary: Ahsan al-Taqasim (985), a systematic survey of every province of the Islamic world from personal travel.

properties.label: Erik the Red
properties.summary: During three years of exile Erik explored the south-west coast of Greenland and chose the fjords that became the Norse settlements.

properties.label: Bjarni
properties.summary: Bjarni, blown off course sailing for Greenland, sighted three unknown lands to the west, the first recorded European sighting of North America.

properties.label: Norse Greenland
properties.summary: The Eastern and Western Settlements of Norse Greenland and their summer hunting grounds (Nordrsetur) north to Disko Bay and Upernavik, where a runestone of c. 1300 was found.

properties.label: Leif Erikson
properties.summary: Leif sailed to Helluland (Baffin Island), Markland (Labrador) and Vinland, wintering at Leifsbudir, probably in northern Newfoundland.

properties.label: Polynesian Outliers
properties.summary: Polynesian voyagers sailed back west to settle Tuvalu and the Outliers such as Tikopia, Rennell, Ontong Java, Kapingamarangi and Nukuoro.

properties.label: Karlsefni
properties.summary: Karlsefni's attempt to settle Vinland with about 160 people explored south into the Gulf of St Lawrence (Straumfjord and Hop) before conflict with the Skraelings ended it.

properties.label: al-Biruni
properties.summary: Followed the Ghaznavid court to Ghazni and the Punjab; measured the earth at Nandana and learned Sanskrit for his Kitab al-Hind (1030).

properties.label: Society Islands
properties.summary: The first settlement of East Polynesia, in the Society Islands (Tahiti, Raiatea), after the long pause in Samoa and Tonga.

properties.label: Kitab al-Hind
properties.summary: Northern India from the Punjab to the Ganges and Malwa, described from Sanskrit learning in al-Biruni's India.

properties.label: Ingvar
properties.summary: Large Swedish expedition east to Serkland (the Muslim lands round the Caspian) that ended in disaster in 1041, commemorated on some 26 Ingvar runestones.

properties.label: al-Bakri: Ghana
properties.summary: Book of Roads and Kingdoms describing Awdaghust, Takrur, Silla, the royal town of Ghana, Kawkaw (Gao) and Tadmekka.

properties.label: Adam of Bremen's North
properties.summary: Adam of Bremen's history (c. 1075) described the Baltic, Sweden, Norway to Halogaland, the Gulf of Bothnia, Estonia, Iceland, Greenland and, for the first time in a European book, Vinland.

properties.leader: First Crusade (Godfrey of Bouillon and others)
properties.label: First Crusade
properties.summary: Crusader armies marched from the Rhineland down the Danube to Constantinople and across Anatolia to Antioch and Jerusalem, and their chronicles gave Western readers first-hand geography of Anatolia and Syria.

properties.label: Baldwin to Edessa
properties.summary: Baldwin left the main army, crossed the Euphrates and took Edessa, founding the first crusader state in upper Mesopotamia.

properties.label: Contact with the Americas
properties.summary: Contact with the Pacific coast of South America, attested by the pre-Columbian sweet potato in Polynesia and by Native American DNA in East Polynesians.

properties.label: al-Idrisi: Africa
properties.summary: The Sahel from Takrur to Kanem, Nubia, Abyssinia and the east African coast to Sofala as shown on the Tabula Rogeriana.

properties.label: al-Idrisi: Europe
properties.summary: Western, northern and eastern Europe (Britain, Norway, the Baltic, Poland, Rus) charted for Roger II from informants at Palermo.

properties.label: Benjamin of Tudela
properties.summary: Benjamin's itinerary described some 300 cities from Spain through Italy, Greece, Constantinople, the Levant, Baghdad and Persia to Egypt, with hearsay of Arabia, India and China.

properties.label: Ibn Jubayr: to Alexandria
properties.summary: Sailed on a Genoese ship from Ceuta past Sardinia, Sicily and Crete to Alexandria in 1183.

properties.label: Ibn Jubayr: Mecca to Acre
properties.summary: Up the Nile and across the Red Sea to Mecca, then by the pilgrim caravan to Baghdad, Mosul, Aleppo, Damascus and Crusader Acre.

properties.label: Ibn Jubayr: return
properties.summary: From Acre on a Christian ship, wrecked at Messina, through Norman Sicily to Cartagena in 1185.

properties.leader: Settlement of the Austral Islands and Rapa
properties.label: Australs, Rapa
properties.summary: Settlement of Rurutu, Tubuai, Raivavae and remote Rapa Iti south of Tahiti.

properties.label: Cook Islands
properties.summary: Settlement of the southern Cook Islands (Aitutaki, Rarotonga, Mangaia) from the Society Islands.

properties.label: Marquesas
properties.summary: Settlement of the Marquesas via the Tuamotus, later a hub for voyages to Hawaii and Rapa Nui.

properties.label: Pitcairn, Henderson
properties.summary: Small Pitcairn and Henderson were settled from Mangareva and traded stone and shell with it.

properties.leader: Settlement of the Tuamotus and Mangareva
properties.label: Tuamotus, Mangareva
properties.summary: Atolls of the Tuamotus and the high islands of Mangareva (Gambier), a gateway to Pitcairn and Rapa Nui.

properties.label: Svalbard found
properties.summary: Icelandic annals record 'Svalbard found' in 1194, a land four days' sail north of Iceland, probably Jan Mayen or the east coast of Greenland.

properties.label: Rapa Nui
properties.summary: Settlement of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), the eastern apex of the Polynesian triangle.

properties.label: Hawaii
properties.summary: Settlement of the Hawaiian Islands, probably from the Marquesas and later in contact with Tahiti (Kahiki).

properties.label: Changchun
properties.summary: Daoist master who crossed Mongolia, the Altai and the Tian Shan to Samarkand and met Genghis Khan in the Hindu Kush; recorded in Xiyou ji.

properties.label: Zhu Fan Zhi
properties.summary: Song customs inspector Zhao Rugua described foreign lands from the Philippines and Java to India, Arabia, Zanzibar, Egypt, Sicily and the Maghreb.

properties.leader: Giovanni da Pian del Carpine (with Benedict the Pole)
properties.label: Plano Carpini
properties.summary: Franciscan envoy who crossed the steppe from Kiev via Batu's camp on the Volga to the Mongol court near Karakorum, writing the first European account of the Mongols and Inner Asia.

properties.label: Aotearoa
properties.summary: The last large land mass settled by humans, reached via the Kermadecs; earliest sites such as Wairau Bar date to the late 13th century.

properties.label: Rubruck
properties.summary: Franciscan who travelled from Constantinople across the Crimea and steppe to Mongke Khan at Karakorum and back via Derbent and Armenia; his report first told Europe that the Caspian is a lake and that Cathay was the land of the Seres.

properties.label: Marco Polo
properties.summary: Gave Europe its first detailed description of the Silk Road through Persia, the Pamirs, the Tarim Basin and the Hexi corridor to Kublai Khan's court.

properties.label: Bar Sauma: to Persia
properties.summary: Two Uyghur or Ongud monks from Khanbaliq crossed the Tarim and Khurasan to the Ilkhanate at Maragheh and Baghdad.

properties.label: Polo in China
properties.summary: Described the interior of China from Khanbaliq to Yunnan and the Burmese border, and south through Hangzhou to Zaitun (Quanzhou).

properties.label: Bar Sauma: Europe
properties.summary: First known person from China to reach western Europe: Constantinople, Naples, Rome, Genoa, Paris (Philip IV) and Gascony (Edward I).

properties.label: Vivaldi brothers
properties.summary: Two Genoese galleys sailed out through the Strait of Gibraltar and down the Moroccan Atlantic coast seeking India by sea, and vanished.

properties.label: Polo return
properties.summary: Return overland from Hormuz through Persia to Tabriz and Trebizond on the Black Sea.

properties.label: Zhou Daguan
properties.summary: Yuan embassy from Wenzhou along the coast of Champa to the Mekong mouth; his Customs of Cambodia is the only eyewitness account of Angkor at its height.

properties.label: Zhou Daguan: to Angkor
properties.summary: Up the Mekong and Tonle Sap to Yasodharapura (Angkor), where he lived for about a year.

properties.leader: Polynesian visit to the Auckland Islands
properties.label: Auckland Islands
properties.summary: Southernmost known Polynesian site, on Enderby Island in the subantarctic Auckland Islands, about 465 km south of New Zealand.

properties.label: Kermadecs
properties.summary: Raoul Island, a stepping stone between East Polynesia and New Zealand, was briefly occupied.

properties.label: Norfolk Island
properties.summary: Norfolk Island had a Polynesian settlement at Emily Bay, probably from the Kermadecs or New Zealand, abandoned before 1774.

properties.label: Malocello
properties.summary: Genoese navigator who reached Lanzarote, the first of the Canaries to reappear on a European map (Dulcert, 1339).

properties.label: Odoric
properties.summary: Crossed Armenia and Persia from Trebizond via Tabriz, Sultaniyeh, Kashan, Yazd and Persepolis to Hormuz.

properties.label: Odoric in China
properties.summary: Travelled from Canton and Zaitun up through Fuzhou, Hangzhou and Nanjing and the Grand Canal to Khanbaliq, giving Europe a vivid account of south China.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 1: to Mecca
properties.summary: From Tangier along North Africa to Egypt, up the Nile to Aydhab, then through Palestine and Syria to Mecca.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 2: Iraq, Iran
properties.summary: With the returning Iraqi hajj caravan to Najaf and Basra, then Isfahan, Shiraz, Baghdad, Tabriz and Mosul.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 3: East Africa
properties.summary: Down the Red Sea to Aden and Zeila, along the Swahili coast to Mogadishu, Mombasa and Kilwa, then back via Dhofar, Oman, Hormuz and Bahrain.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 4: Anatolia, steppe
properties.summary: Through Anatolia and across the Black Sea to the Golden Horde, to Constantinople and back, then via Khwarazm, Bukhara, Samarkand and Afghanistan to the Indus.

properties.label: Wang Dayuan
properties.summary: Two merchant voyages whose Daoyi Zhilue (1349) described about 100 places from Temasek (Singapore) to India, Hormuz and the Somali coast.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 5: Sind to Delhi
properties.summary: Sind and Multan to Delhi, where he served Muhammad bin Tughluq, then south through Malwa and Daulatabad to Cambay.

properties.label: Marignolli
properties.summary: Papal embassy across the Golden Horde and Chagatai steppes via Sarai, Almaliq and Hami to Khanbaliq.

properties.leader: Niccoloso da Recco and Angiolino del Tegghia de Corbizzi
properties.label: Recco 1341
properties.summary: Three-ship Portuguese-sponsored expedition that spent five months mapping thirteen islands of the Canaries.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 6: Malabar, Maldives, Bengal
properties.summary: Down the Malabar coast to Calicut, then the Maldives (where he served as qadi), Ceylon and Adam's Peak, Ma'bar and Bengal.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 7: to China
properties.summary: From Bengal via Samudra (Sumatra) and the South China Sea to Zaitun (Quanzhou) and Guangzhou.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 8: return to Hormuz
properties.summary: Back from China via Sumatra, Quilon and Calicut across the Arabian Sea to Dhofar and Hormuz.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 9: home via Mecca
properties.summary: Through Iran, Iraq and Syria during the Black Death to a last hajj at Mecca, then Cairo and Alexandria before sailing west to Fez (1349).

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 10: al-Andalus
properties.summary: Across the strait to Gibraltar, Ronda, Malaga and Nasrid Granada.

properties.label: Ibn Battuta 11: Mali
properties.summary: Across the Sahara via Taghaza and Walata to the capital of Mali, then Timbuktu, Gao and Takedda and back north via Tuwat.

properties.leader: Jean de Bethencourt and Gadifer de La Salle
properties.label: Bethencourt
properties.summary: Norman conquest of Lanzarote, Fuerteventura and El Hierro, described in the chronicle Le Canarien.

properties.label: Clavijo
properties.summary: Castilian embassy to Timur, describing the road from Trebizond through Persia and Khorasan to Samarkand.

properties.label: Isalguier (claimed)
properties.summary: A Toulousain said to have lived eight years at Gao on the Niger and returned with an African wife, but his writings had no effect on European maps.

properties.label: Zheng He 1
properties.summary: Treasure fleet to Champa, Java, Palembang, Malacca, Semudera, Ceylon and Calicut.

properties.label: Zheng He 2
properties.summary: Second fleet visited Siam as well as Java, Malacca, Ceylon, Cochin and Calicut.

properties.label: Zheng He 3
properties.summary: Third voyage to Calicut; on the way home the fleet fought and captured the king of Kotte in Ceylon (1411).

properties.label: Zheng He 4
properties.summary: First fleet beyond India, reaching Hormuz at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.

properties.label: Chen Cheng
properties.summary: Ming embassy to Shahrukh at Herat via Turfan, the Ili, Tashkent and Samarkand; recorded in Xiyu Fanguo Zhi.

properties.label: Zheng He 5
properties.summary: Fleet and detachments reached Hormuz, Aden and the east African ports of Mogadishu, Brava and Malindi.

properties.leader: Joao Goncalves Zarco, Tristao Vaz Teixeira, Bartolomeu Perestrelo
properties.label: Zarco
properties.summary: Portuguese caravels recognised Porto Santo and then Madeira, settled from 1425.

properties.label: Conti
properties.summary: Crossed the Syrian desert from Damascus to Baghdad and went down the Tigris to Basra.

properties.label: Conti in India
properties.summary: Went inland from Cambay to the city of Vijayanagar and across the peninsula to Mylapore.

properties.label: Zheng He 6
properties.summary: Returned foreign envoys home; detachments visited Dhofar, Aden, Mogadishu and Brava.

properties.label: Conti in Burma
properties.summary: From Bengal to Arakan and overland to Ava and Pegu, the first European account of Burma's interior.

properties.label: Silves
properties.summary: Portuguese pilot credited with finding the eastern and possibly central Azores.

properties.label: Goncalo Velho
properties.summary: Found the Formigas rocks and Santa Maria, beginning the official Portuguese discovery of the Azores.

properties.label: Zheng He 7
properties.summary: Last voyage to Hormuz; a detachment with Ma Huan sailed up the Red Sea to Jeddah for Mecca.

properties.label: Gil Eanes
properties.summary: First recorded European ship to pass Cape Bojador and return, opening the Saharan coast.

properties.leader: Gil Eanes and Afonso Goncalves Baldaia
properties.label: Angra dos Ruivos
properties.summary: Sailed 30 to 50 leagues beyond Bojador to the bay they named Angra dos Ruivos.

properties.label: Baldaia
properties.summary: Named the Rio do Ouro inlet (Dakhla) and crossed the Tropic of Cancer to Pedra da Gale off Cape Barbas.

properties.label: Nuno Tristao 1441
properties.summary: Reached Cape Blanc (Ras Nouadhibou).

properties.label: Nuno Tristao 1443
properties.summary: Reached the Bay of Arguin and Arguin island.

properties.label: Nuno Tristao 1445
properties.summary: Reached the Langue de Barbarie near the mouth of the Senegal River, the edge of the Sahel.

properties.label: Nuno Tristao 1446
properties.summary: Passed Cap Vert to a large river, probably in the Sine-Saloum delta, where he was killed.

properties.label: Malfante
properties.summary: Genoese merchant whose 1447 letter from the Tuat oasis gave Europe its first eyewitness report of the Sahara trade and hearsay of Timbuktu and the Niger.

properties.label: Chatham Islands
properties.summary: Moriori ancestors from New Zealand settled the Chatham Islands, 800 km east of the mainland.

properties.label: Cadamosto 1455
properties.summary: Venetian in Henry's service who described Senegal, Cayor and the Gambia mouth in his widely printed Navigazioni.

properties.label: Cadamosto 1456
properties.summary: Reported the Cape Verde Islands (Boa Vista, Santiago), went up the Gambia to Badibu and on to the Geba estuary and Bissagos.

properties.label: Cadamosto up the Gambia
properties.summary: Sailed about 60 Italian miles up the Gambia to visit the ruler he called Battimansa in Badibu.

properties.label: Diogo Gomes 1456
properties.summary: Reached the Rio Grande (Geba) and then sailed some 50 leagues up the Gambia to the Mali gold market of Cantor.

properties.label: Gomes up the Gambia
properties.summary: Went about 50 leagues up the Gambia to Cantor, a market town for Mali gold.

properties.leader: Diogo Gomes and Antonio de Noli
properties.label: Diogo Gomes 1462
properties.summary: Traded in the Saloum delta and landed on and named Santiago in the Cape Verde Islands.

properties.label: Ibn Majid
properties.summary: Kitab al-Fawa'id (c. 1490), a pilot's manual of Indian Ocean sea routes, star altitudes and coasts from the Gulf to Malacca.

properties.label: Pedro de Sintra
properties.summary: Charted the coast of Sierra Leone and Liberia past Cape Mount and Cape Mesurado to the Bosco de Santa Maria.

properties.label: Nikitin
properties.summary: From Tver down the Volga, round the Caspian and across Persia to Hormuz, the first Russian account of the route to India.

properties.label: Nikitin in India
properties.summary: Described the Deccan interior: Junnar, the Bahmani capital Bidar and the shrine of Parvattum.

properties.label: Fernao do Po
properties.summary: First European to reach Bioko (Formosa, later Fernando Po) and the Cameroon coast at the head of the Gulf of Guinea.

properties.label: Nikitin return
properties.summary: Returned from Hormuz across Persia and eastern Anatolia to Trebizond, then from Caffa north towards Smolensk, where he died.

properties.label: Diogo Cao I
properties.summary: Found the mouth of the Congo and followed the Angolan coast to Cabo de Santa Maria, setting stone padroes.

properties.label: Diogo Cao II
properties.summary: Second voyage carrying the coast survey on to Cabo Negro and Cape Cross in Namibia.

properties.label: Cão up the Congo
properties.summary: Portuguese boats ascended the Congo estuary to the Yellala falls, leaving a carved inscription, the first European penetration of the river.

properties.leader: Pero da Covilha and Afonso de Paiva
properties.label: Covilha (Egypt)
properties.summary: Royal spies sent to find the spice routes and Prester John crossed Egypt from Alexandria via Cairo to the Red Sea.

properties.label: Covilha (Indian Ocean)
properties.summary: Travelling on Arab and Indian trading vessels he saw Aden, Calicut, Goa, Hormuz and the Swahili coast to Sofala, reporting the Indian Ocean trade to Lisbon.

properties.label: Bartolomeu Dias
properties.summary: Rounded the southern tip of Africa unseen, landed at Mossel Bay, reached Kwaaihoek and sighted the Cape of Good Hope on the way home.

properties.label: Sousa to Mbanza Kongo
properties.summary: Portuguese embassy marched from Mpinda at the Congo mouth to the Kongo capital Mbanza Kongo, opening the kingdom to European description.

properties.label: Columbus I
properties.summary: First European crossing to the Bahamas, Cuba and Hispaniola, opening the Caribbean to European knowledge.

properties.label: Covilhã
properties.summary: Portuguese envoy who, after scouting Cairo, Aden, India and Sofala, went inland from Zeila to the Ethiopian court and never left.

properties.label: Covilha to Zeila
properties.summary: After revisiting Aden, Hormuz and Jeddah he crossed the Red Sea from Sinai to Zeila on the Somali coast.

properties.label: Columbus II
properties.summary: Charted the Lesser Antilles, Puerto Rico, Jamaica and the south coast of Cuba.

properties.label: Covilha to Ethiopia
properties.summary: Went inland from Zeila to the court of the Ethiopian emperor Eskender, where he spent the rest of his life.

properties.label: Cabot
properties.summary: English landfall in Newfoundland, the first recorded European visit to mainland North America since the Norse.

properties.label: Vasco da Gama
properties.summary: First sea voyage from Europe to India, charting the Natal and Swahili coasts and crossing the Arabian Sea to Calicut.

properties.label: Columbus III
properties.summary: First European sighting of the South American mainland at Trinidad, the Gulf of Paria and the Orinoco outflow.

properties.leader: Alonso de Ojeda, Juan de la Cosa, Amerigo Vespucci
properties.label: Ojeda
properties.summary: Followed the Venezuelan coast from the Orinoco to the Guajira, naming the Gulf of Venezuela and Lake Maracaibo.

properties.label: Pinzon
properties.summary: First European landfall in Brazil and first entry into the Amazon estuary, the 'Mar Dulce'.

properties.label: Cabral
properties.summary: Second India fleet: made the first recorded European landfall in Brazil (Monte Pascoal, Porto Seguro), then reached Sofala, Kilwa, Calicut and Cochin.

properties.label: Diogo Dias
properties.summary: Separated from Cabral, he sighted Madagascar (Sao Lourenco), sailed past Cape Guardafui into the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea mouth.

properties.label: Vespucci
properties.summary: Followed the Brazilian coast south to Rio de Janeiro and Cananeia, convincing Vespucci it was a new continent.

properties.label: Joao da Nova
properties.summary: Third India fleet, credited with finding Ascension on the way out and St Helena on the way home.

properties.label: Columbus IV
properties.summary: Coasted Central America from Honduras to Panama, adding the Caribbean shore of the isthmus to the map.

properties.leader: Estevao da Gama's squadron of Vasco da Gama's 4th India fleet (account by Thome Lopes)
properties.label: Thome Lopes
properties.summary: Eyewitness account of the 1502 to 1503 India voyage, describing St Helena as an unknown island on 30 July 1503 and mentioning Ascension.

properties.label: Fernandes Pereira
properties.summary: Sailed alone by the outer route east of Madagascar to Cape Guardafui and became the first Portuguese to reach and winter on Socotra.

properties.label: Varthema
properties.summary: First known non-Muslim European to describe Medina and Mecca, travelling with the Damascus Hajj caravan, then explored Yemen from Aden to Sanaa.

properties.label: Varthema in Persia
properties.summary: Travelled inland from Hormuz to Herat and Shiraz with a Persian merchant partner.

properties.label: Tristao da Cunha
properties.summary: Sighted the remote South Atlantic islands that bear his name, then raided the Swahili coast and took Socotra.

properties.label: Mascarenes
properties.summary: Sent by Tristao da Cunha to explore around Madagascar, he found Reunion (Santa Apolonia), Mauritius (Cirne) and Rodrigues.

properties.label: Albuquerque to Hormuz
properties.summary: Followed the Omani coast from Ras al Hadd via Qalhat, Muscat and Sohar into the Persian Gulf to Hormuz.

properties.label: Sequeira
properties.summary: First Portuguese fleet to reach Malacca, after calling on Sumatra's northern ports.

properties.label: Leo Africanus
properties.summary: His Description of Africa, written in Italy and printed by Ramusio in 1550, shaped European knowledge of Timbuktu and the Sahel for centuries.

properties.leader: Antonio de Abreu and Francisco Serrao
properties.label: Abreu to Banda
properties.summary: First European fleet to the Banda Islands, following the north coast of Java and the Lesser Sunda chain.

properties.label: Albuquerque to Malacca
properties.summary: Captured Malacca, from which embassies and fleets went to Siam, Pegu, the Spice Islands and China.

properties.label: Fernandes
properties.summary: A Portuguese degredado who walked inland from Sofala to Manica and the Mutapa state, the first European report of the Zimbabwe plateau.

properties.label: Serrao to Ternate
properties.summary: Shipwrecked survivors rescued by local rulers were taken into the Moluccas, where Serrao stayed and sent news of the clove islands.

properties.label: Albuquerque Red Sea
properties.summary: First European fleet in the Red Sea; failed to take Aden and reached Kamaran island.

properties.label: Jorge Alvares
properties.summary: First Portuguese to reach China by sea, landing at Tamao in the Pearl River delta.

properties.label: Balboa
properties.summary: First Europeans to see the Pacific from the Americas, after crossing the Isthmus of Darien.

properties.label: Piri Reis map
properties.summary: Ottoman world map compiled from Portuguese, Spanish and Columbus charts, showing the Atlantic, West Africa, Brazil and the Caribbean.

properties.label: Ponce de Leon
properties.summary: First recorded European exploration of Florida's Atlantic coast, Keys and Gulf coast.

properties.label: Solis
properties.summary: Discovered the Rio de la Plata estuary, opening the way to the Parana and Uruguay rivers.

properties.leader: Fernao Pires de Andrade (with Tome Pires)
properties.label: Andrade to Canton
properties.summary: First official Portuguese mission to China, sailing up the Pearl River to Canton.

properties.label: Cordoba
properties.summary: First European expedition to the Maya coast of Yucatan, reaching Campeche and Champoton.

properties.label: Grijalva
properties.summary: Followed the Gulf coast of Mexico from Cozumel past Tabasco to Veracruz, bringing first news of the Aztec state.

properties.label: Cortes
properties.summary: March from the Gulf coast to Tenochtitlan, revealing the Valley of Mexico and the Aztec capital to Europe.

properties.label: Magellan
properties.summary: Charted the Patagonian coast and found the strait to the Pacific (Atlantic and strait leg only).

properties.label: Pineda
properties.summary: First map of the whole northern Gulf of Mexico coast, from Florida to Veracruz, including the Mississippi mouth.

properties.leader: Francisco Álvares (embassy of Rodrigo de Lima)
properties.label: Álvares
properties.summary: Six-year Portuguese embassy to Lebna Dengel whose printed narrative (1540) gave Europe the first detailed descriptions of Aksum and Lalibela.

properties.label: Magellan
properties.summary: First European crossing of the Pacific, revealing its width, the Marianas and the Philippines, and reaching the Moluccas from the east.

properties.label: Sequeira Red Sea
properties.summary: Governor's Red Sea campaign that landed the first official Portuguese embassy to Ethiopia.

properties.label: Trinidad
properties.summary: Failed attempt by the Trinidad to sail back east across the North Pacific, reaching about 42 or 43 degrees N before scurvy forced a return.

properties.label: Alvarado
properties.summary: Conquest route into highland Guatemala and Cuzcatlan (El Salvador).

properties.label: Cortes to Honduras
properties.summary: Overland march across Tabasco and the Peten to Honduras, crossing the Maya lowlands.

properties.label: Gomes
properties.summary: Surveyed the coast from Florida to Nova Scotia for Spain, ascending the Penobscot and naming the Hudson the Rio de San Antonio.

properties.label: Verrazzano
properties.summary: First survey of the North American Atlantic coast from the Carolinas to Newfoundland, including New York Bay.

properties.leader: Garcia Jofre de Loaisa; Toribio Alonso de Salazar
properties.label: Loaisa
properties.summary: Second Spanish fleet through the Strait of Magellan; its flagship crossed the Pacific via Bokak atoll and Guam to Mindanao and the Moluccas.

properties.leader: Francisco Pizarro, Diego de Almagro, Bartolome Ruiz
properties.label: Pizarro voyage
properties.summary: Sailed down the Pacific coast of Colombia and Ecuador to Tumbes, the first European contact with the Inca state.

properties.label: Saavedra
properties.summary: First crossing from Mexico to the Moluccas; its return attempts ran along the north coast of New Guinea to the Admiralties and Marshalls.

properties.label: Cabeza de Vaca
properties.summary: Eight-year odyssey of four survivors across Texas and northern Mexico, the first European account of the region.

properties.label: Narvaez
properties.summary: Overland march through northern Florida to Apalachee, then raft voyage along the Gulf coast to Texas.

properties.label: Pizarro
properties.summary: Conquest route from Tumbes to Cajamarca and along the Inca road to Cusco, opening the Andes to Europe.

properties.label: Belalcazar
properties.summary: From Piura to Quito, then north through the Cauca valley to Popayan, Cali and the Bogota plateau.

properties.label: Cartier I
properties.summary: Mapped the Gulf of St Lawrence, Prince Edward Island, Chaleur Bay and Gaspe.

properties.label: Almagro
properties.summary: First European expedition into Chile, via the Altiplano and northwest Argentina over the Andes to Copiapo and the Itata.

properties.label: Cartier II
properties.summary: Ascended the St Lawrence to Stadacona (Quebec) and Hochelaga (Montreal); returned by the Cabot Strait.

properties.label: Federmann
properties.summary: Crossed the Venezuelan and Colombian llanos along the foot of the Andes and climbed to Bogota.

properties.label: Quesada
properties.summary: Up the Magdalena and onto the Muisca highlands, revealing the Bogota plateau, Tunja and Sogamoso.

properties.label: Mendes Pinto
properties.summary: Adventurer whose Peregrinacao (1614) gave Europe a sweeping, if embroidered, picture of the Red Sea, Malacca, Siam, Pegu, China and Japan.

properties.leader: Hernando de Soto (then Luis de Moscoso)
properties.label: De Soto
properties.summary: Four-year march across the American Southeast, crossing the Mississippi and reaching east Texas.

properties.label: Ulloa
properties.summary: Showed Baja California to be a peninsula by sailing to the head of the Gulf of California and round to Cedros Island.

properties.label: Grand Canyon
properties.summary: First Europeans at the Grand Canyon, reaching the South Rim near Desert View.

properties.leader: Joao de Castro (in Estevao da Gama's fleet)
properties.label: Joao de Castro
properties.summary: Expedition to Suez whose Roteiro do Mar Roxo was the first detailed European survey of the Red Sea coasts, with charts and views.

properties.label: Coronado
properties.summary: Searched for Cibola and Quivira, revealing the Pueblo world, the Llano Estacado and the Great Plains as far as Kansas.

properties.label: Valdivia
properties.summary: Marched through the Atacama to found Santiago, then pushed south to Concepcion, Valdivia and Villarrica.

properties.leader: Cristóvão da Gama (account by Miguel de Castanhoso)
properties.label: da Gama in Ethiopia
properties.summary: Portuguese musketeers marched from Massawa through Tigray to Lake Tana's battlefields; Castanhoso's account (1564) described the highlands.

properties.label: Orellana
properties.summary: First descent of the Amazon from the Napo to the Atlantic, naming the Rio Negro.

properties.label: Cabrillo
properties.summary: First European voyage along the coast of Alta California, from San Diego Bay to near Point Reyes.

properties.label: Villalobos
properties.summary: Crossed from New Spain to Mindanao and named the islands Filipinas; Inigo Ortiz de Retes then followed the north coast of New Guinea and named it Nueva Guinea (1545).

properties.leader: Antonio Mota and Francisco Zeimoto (Portuguese traders)
properties.label: Portuguese reach Japan
properties.summary: First Europeans to reach Japan, landing on Tanegashima and introducing firearms.

properties.label: Pastene
properties.summary: Naval reconnaissance of the Chilean coast south of Valparaiso to about 41 S.

properties.label: Xavier to Japan
properties.summary: Jesuit mission that landed at Kagoshima, beginning the Jesuit letters that described Japan to Europe.

properties.label: Seydi Ali Reis: fleet
properties.summary: Took the Ottoman Basra squadron out of the Gulf; after battles with the Portuguese off Oman and a storm it was wrecked on the Gujarat coast.

properties.label: Seydi Ali Reis: overland home
properties.summary: Mirat ul-Memalik: overland from Gujarat through Sind, Mughal Delhi, Kabul, Transoxiana and Safavid Iran back to Istanbul.

properties.label: Jenkinson
properties.summary: Englishman who went down the Volga, across the Caspian and the Ustyurt desert via Urgench to Bukhara; his 1562 map of Russia and Tartary followed.

properties.leader: Pedro de Ursua, Lope de Aguirre
properties.label: Ursua/Aguirre
properties.summary: Descent of the Huallaga, Maranon and Amazon in search of Omagua and El Dorado, ending in Aguirre's revolt in Venezuela.

properties.label: Legazpi
properties.summary: Crossing from New Spain via the Marshalls and Guam to Samar and Cebu, founding the Spanish Philippines.

properties.leader: Andres de Urdaneta; Felipe de Salcedo
properties.label: Tornaviaje
properties.summary: The tornaviaje: first west to east crossing of the Pacific, via the westerlies near 38 N, opening the Manila galleon route.

properties.label: Mendana
properties.summary: Discovered the Solomon Islands (Santa Isabel, Guadalcanal, Malaita, Makira) and returned via the Marshalls and Wake to Mexico.

properties.label: Barreto on the Zambezi
properties.summary: Portuguese army ascended the Zambezi to Sena and campaigned inland, establishing the river route into Mutapa lands.

properties.leader: Portuguese Macau to Nagasaki trade ship (nau do trato)
properties.label: Macau to Nagasaki
properties.summary: Portuguese helped found the port of Nagasaki with daimyo Omura Sumitada, the terminus of annual ships from Macau.

properties.label: Frobisher
properties.summary: Entered Frobisher Bay on Baffin Island (1576 to 1578) and in 1578 sailed some way into Hudson Strait.

properties.label: Yermak
properties.summary: Cossack raid over the Urals by the Chusovaya, Tagil, Tura and Tobol to Qashliq, capital of the Khanate of Sibir, opening western Siberia to Russia.

properties.label: Linschoten out
properties.summary: Dutch secretary to the Archbishop of Goa whose Itinerario (1596) published Portuguese sailing directions to the East.

properties.label: Davis
properties.summary: Charted south-west Greenland and Cumberland Sound, and in 1587 sailed up Davis Strait to 72 12 N (Hope Sanderson).

properties.label: Linschoten home
properties.summary: Return voyage via St Helena and two years on Terceira in the Azores before reaching Lisbon and Enkhuizen.

properties.label: Lancaster 1591
properties.summary: First English voyage to the Indian Ocean, via Zanzibar and Cape Comorin to Penang and Ceylon.

properties.label: Houtman
properties.summary: First Dutch voyage to the East Indies, reaching Bantam, the north Java coast, Madura and Bali.

properties.leader: Alvaro de Mendana; Pedro Fernandes de Queiros
properties.label: Mendana 2
properties.summary: Discovered the Marquesas and the Santa Cruz Islands; after Mendana's death Queiros took the survivors to Manila.

properties.label: Raleigh
properties.summary: Ascended the Orinoco via the Manamo channel to the Caroni, producing 'The Discovery of Guiana'.

properties.label: Barentsz
properties.summary: Discovered Bear Island and Spitsbergen, rounded the north of Novaya Zemlya and survived the first Arctic wintering, escaping by open boat to Kola.

properties.label: Houtman to Aceh
properties.summary: Zeeland voyage to Aceh where Cornelis was killed and Frederick imprisoned, later publishing a Malay-Dutch dictionary and southern star catalogue.

properties.label: Van Neck
properties.summary: Second Dutch fleet; van Neck's ships resupplied on Madagascar's east coast and loaded spices at Bantam.

properties.label: Warwijck
properties.summary: Part of the second Dutch fleet that landed on and named Mauritius, then sailed via Ambon to Ternate.

properties.label: Heemskerck
properties.summary: Reached Great Banda and left 22 men to buy nutmeg, the first Dutch post in the Bandas.

properties.label: Van Neck to China
properties.summary: Brought the first Dutch ships to the China coast, at Macau, where Portuguese forces killed his landing parties.

properties.label: EIC first voyage
properties.summary: First East India Company fleet: Table Bay, Antongil Bay in Madagascar, the Nicobars, Aceh, Priaman and Bantam, where the first English factory was set up.

properties.label: Goes
properties.summary: Overland from Agra via Kabul, the Pamirs, Yarkand and the Tarim towns to Suzhou (Jiuquan), proving that Cathay was China.

properties.label: Champlain 1603
properties.summary: Re-examined the St Lawrence from Tadoussac to the Lachine rapids.

properties.label: Páez
properties.summary: Spanish Jesuit who settled at Gorgora on Lake Tana and on 21 April 1618 visited the springs of the Blue Nile at Gish Abay.

properties.leader: Samuel de Champlain, Pierre Dugua de Mons
properties.label: Champlain Acadia
properties.summary: Surveyed the Bay of Fundy and the coast of Maine and Massachusetts as far as Cape Cod.

properties.label: Van den Broecke (Angola)
properties.summary: Dutch merchant whose journal of trading voyages to Cape Verde, Guinea and Angola was published in 1634.

properties.label: Duyfken
properties.summary: First recorded European landfall on Australia, charting the west coast of Cape York in the Gulf of Carpentaria.

properties.label: Queiros
properties.summary: Searched for Terra Australis, crossing the Tuamotus to Taumako and Espiritu Santo (Vanuatu), then returned to Acapulco.

properties.label: Torres
properties.summary: Sailed west along the south coast of New Guinea and through Torres Strait, proving New Guinea was not part of a southern continent.

properties.label: Hudson
properties.summary: Sought a polar route: in 1607 along east Greenland to Spitsbergen at 80 N (finding Jan Mayen area waters), in 1608 to Novaya Zemlya.

properties.label: Lake Champlain
properties.summary: Up the Richelieu to the lake later named Lake Champlain.

properties.label: Hudson River
properties.summary: Ascended the Hudson River to near Albany, laying the basis for New Netherland.

properties.label: Hudson Bay
properties.summary: Passed through Hudson Strait into Hudson Bay and down the east coast to James Bay.

properties.label: Button
properties.summary: Crossed Hudson Bay to winter at the Nelson River, then charted the west coast north to about 65 N.

properties.label: Van den Broecke (Aden)
properties.summary: First Dutch merchant in Arabia, at Aden and al-Shihr in Hadramawt, where Dutch traders were left to learn Arabic.

properties.label: Bylot and Baffin
properties.summary: Explored Foxe Channel along Southampton Island, showing no western outlet from Hudson Bay.

properties.label: Champlain Huronia
properties.summary: Via the Ottawa River and Lake Nipissing to Georgian Bay and Huronia, then across Lake Ontario into Iroquois country.

properties.label: Baffin
properties.summary: Circuited Baffin Bay, finding Smith, Jones and Lancaster sounds and reaching 77 45 N.

properties.label: Bocarro
properties.summary: Portuguese trader who walked from Tete past the south end of Lake Malawi to Kilwa on the Swahili coast.

properties.label: Van den Broecke (Mocha, Surat)
properties.summary: Tried to open a Dutch post at Mocha (where he tasted coffee), then founded the VOC establishment at Surat.

properties.label: Hartog
properties.summary: Landed on Dirk Hartog Island and charted the Western Australian coast north to about 22 S (Eendrachtsland).

properties.label: Le Maire
properties.summary: Opened the Le Maire Strait and Cape Horn route and crossed the Pacific via the Tuamotus, northern Tonga and Futuna to New Ireland and New Guinea.

properties.label: Munk
properties.summary: Danish expedition through Hudson Strait to winter at the Churchill River mouth on Hudson Bay; only three survived.

properties.label: Pyanda
properties.summary: First Russians to reach the Lena, going up the Lower Tunguska and down the Lena towards the site of Yakutsk, returning by the Angara.

properties.label: Carstenszoon
properties.summary: Charted the south coast of New Guinea (sighting its snow peaks) and the east side of the Gulf of Carpentaria to the Staaten River.

properties.leader: Antonio de Andrade and Manuel Marques
properties.label: Andrade
properties.summary: First Europeans known to enter Tibet, crossing the Mana Pass to Tsaparang, capital of Guge.

properties.label: Lobo
properties.summary: Jesuit who crossed the Danakil from Beilul to Tigray, visited the Blue Nile source in 1629 and left via Massawa; his account reached Europe in French (1728) and Johnson's English (1735).

properties.label: Cacella
properties.summary: First Europeans in Bhutan, continuing over the Himalaya to Shigatse in central Tibet.

properties.label: Thijssen
properties.summary: Charted about 1,500 km of the southern coast of Australia from Cape Leeuwin to the Nuyts Archipelago.

properties.label: Beketov
properties.summary: From Yeniseysk up the Angara and Ilim, over the portage to the Lena, and down it to found the Yakutsk ostrog in 1632.

properties.label: Teixeira
properties.summary: First European ascent of the whole Amazon, to Quito, and back; Cristobal de Acuna's account followed.

properties.label: Moskvitin
properties.summary: First Russians to reach the Pacific, by the Aldan, Maya and Ulya rivers to the Sea of Okhotsk.

properties.label: Perfilyev
properties.summary: Sailed up the Vitim to the Tsipa, the first Russian to enter Transbaikalia (Dauria).

properties.label: Stadukhin
properties.summary: Down the Indigirka to the Arctic and east along the coast to the Kolyma, where the first ostrog was built.

properties.label: Tasman
properties.summary: Discovered Van Diemen's Land (Tasmania), the west coast of New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji, proving Australia did not join a southern continent.

properties.label: Poyarkov
properties.summary: First Russian descent of the Amur: up the Aldan and Gonam, over the Stanovoy range, down the Zeya and Amur to its mouth, then along the Okhotsk coast and back by the Maya.

properties.label: Tasman 2
properties.summary: Charted the north coast of Australia from Cape York round the Gulf of Carpentaria and Arnhem Land to the north-west coast, as one continuous New Holland.

properties.label: Dezhnev
properties.summary: Sailed from the Kolyma round the eastern tip of Asia through the strait later named for Bering, proving Asia and America were separated.

properties.label: Dezhnev on foot
properties.summary: Survivors walked from the wreck to the Anadyr mouth and went upriver to found winter quarters near Anadyrsk.

properties.label: Raposo Tavares
properties.summary: Bandeira from Sao Paulo across the Paraguay basin to the Andes foothills and down the Madeira and Amazon.

properties.label: Khabarov
properties.summary: Up the Olyokma and Tungir to the Shilka and Amur, built Albazin and sailed down the Amur past the Sungari to near modern Khabarovsk.

properties.label: Stadukhin overland
properties.summary: Opened the overland route from the Kolyma via the Anyuy to the Anadyr, then reached the Penzhina and followed the north coast of the Sea of Okhotsk to Okhotsk.

properties.leader: Hendrick Hamel and the Sperwer crew
properties.label: Hamel
properties.summary: Shipwrecked Dutch sailors held in Korea for 13 years; Hamel's journal was Europe's first first-hand account of Joseon Korea.

properties.label: Grueber
properties.summary: Peking to Agra by Xining, the Kokonor and Lhasa, then over the Himalaya to Kathmandu, the first Europeans in Lhasa.

properties.label: Evliya Celebi: Vienna
properties.summary: Accompanied Kara Mehmed Pasha's embassy to Vienna and described the Habsburg capital in the Seyahatname.

properties.label: Evliya Celebi: Nile
properties.summary: Travelled up the Nile through Ottoman Egypt and Nubia towards the Funj sultanate of Sennar.

properties.label: Marquette and Jolliet
properties.summary: Down the Fox-Wisconsin route and the Mississippi to the Arkansas mouth, proving the river drains to the Gulf.

properties.label: Le Griffon
properties.summary: First sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes, through Lakes Erie, Huron and Michigan to Green Bay.

properties.label: La Salle
properties.summary: Descended the Illinois and Mississippi to the Gulf of Mexico and claimed Louisiana for France.

properties.label: Atlasov
properties.summary: First systematic Russian exploration of Kamchatka, from Anadyrsk down both coasts and the Kamchatka river to the Golygina.

properties.label: Dampier
properties.summary: Surveyed Shark Bay and the north-west coast of Australia, then found New Britain and the strait between it and New Guinea.

properties.label: Tulisen to the Kalmyks
properties.summary: Qing embassy across Mongolia and Siberia to Ayuka Khan of the Kalmyks on the lower Volga; described in Yiyu lu (1723).

properties.label: Desideri
properties.summary: Delhi to Kashmir, Ladakh and across western Tibet past Kailash to Lhasa, followed by the fullest early European study of Tibet.

properties.leader: Kangxi atlas survey (Huangyu Quanlan Tu, base-like)
properties.label: Kangxi atlas
properties.summary: Jesuit and Chinese survey of the whole Qing realm (1708 to 1717), with lama surveyors mapping Tibet to Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar.

properties.label: Messerschmidt
properties.summary: First scientific expedition through Siberia, from Tobolsk via Tomsk, the Yenisei and Lower Tunguska to Irkutsk and Dauria.

properties.label: Qing to Lhasa
properties.summary: Qing armies from Kokonor and Sichuan expelled the Dzungars and occupied Lhasa.

properties.label: Desideri return
properties.summary: Left Lhasa by Kuti on the Nepal border and returned via the Ganges plain to Agra.

properties.label: Roggeveen
properties.summary: Found Easter Island (5 April 1722), islands of the Tuamotus and Society group (Bora Bora, Maupiti) and Samoa.

properties.label: Bering 1
properties.summary: First Kamchatka Expedition: sailed north along Kamchatka and Chukotka through the Bering Strait to 67 18 N.

properties.leader: Johann Georg Gmelin and Gerhard Friedrich Muller
properties.label: Gmelin and Muller
properties.sponsor: Russian Academy of Sciences (Great Northern Expedition)
properties.summary: Academic land party of the Great Northern Expedition, surveying western and southern Siberia, Baikal and Dauria before reaching Yakutsk.

properties.leader: Jesuit surveyors for the Kangxi Emperor (Regis, Jartoux, Fridelli and others)
properties.label: Kangxi atlas
properties.summary: The Jesuit-Qing triangulation survey of China, Manchuria and Korea (1708-1718) reached European readers through Du Halde (1735) and d'Anville's atlas, replacing guesswork with measured maps.

properties.label: Malygin
properties.summary: Western detachment of the Great Northern Expedition: charted the Kara Sea coast from the Pechora past Yamal to the Ob estuary.

properties.label: Krasheninnikov
properties.sponsor: Russian Academy of Sciences (Great Northern Expedition)
properties.summary: Spent four years exploring Kamchatka; his Description of Kamchatka (1755) was Europe's first full account of the peninsula and its Itelmen people.

properties.label: La Verendrye
properties.summary: From Fort La Reine to the Mandan villages on the upper Missouri.

properties.label: D. Laptev
properties.summary: Charted the Arctic coast from the Lena delta past the Indigirka to the Kolyma, then went overland to the Anadyr.

properties.label: Kh. Laptev
properties.summary: Sailed the Laptev Sea coast from the Lena to the Khatanga Gulf; his sledge survey of the Taymyr is included in chelyuskin-1742.

properties.label: Bering
properties.summary: Second Kamchatka Expedition: first European sighting of north-west America (Mount Saint Elias, Kayak Island) and of the Aleutian chain.

properties.label: Chelyuskin
properties.summary: Sledge surveys of the Taymyr Peninsula: Khariton Laptev along the west coast (1741) and Chelyuskin to Cape Chelyuskin, the northernmost point of Eurasia (May 1742).

properties.label: Chirikov
properties.summary: Reached the Alexander Archipelago of southeast Alaska, the first European sighting of the Northwest Coast there.

properties.label: Verendrye brothers
properties.summary: First Europeans on the northern Great Plains west of the Missouri, sighting the Rockies (probably the Bighorns).

properties.label: La Condamine
properties.summary: First scientific map of the Amazon, descending from the Maranon through the Pongo de Manseriche to Para.

properties.label: Henday
properties.summary: First European to reach the Alberta plains and meet the Blackfoot, near present Red Deer.

properties.leader: Qing conquest of Dzungaria and the Tarim
properties.label: Qing to Ili and Kashgar
properties.summary: Qing conquest of the Dzungar Khanate and Altishahr, followed by Jesuit-assisted surveys of the new territory.

properties.label: Niebuhr Yemen
properties.summary: Scientific expedition that mapped Yemen from the Tihama to Sanaa; Niebuhr was its only survivor.

properties.label: Byron
properties.summary: Fast circumnavigation crossing the Tuamotus (Disappointment Islands), Tokelau and Kiribati (Nikunau) to Tinian.

properties.label: Niebuhr return
properties.summary: Overland return from the Gulf via Shiraz and Persepolis (where he copied cuneiform), Babylon, Baghdad, Mosul and Aleppo to Constantinople.

properties.label: Carteret
properties.summary: Discovered Pitcairn Island and St George's Channel, separating New Ireland from New Britain.

properties.label: Wallis
properties.summary: First European visit to Tahiti (June 1767), adding the Tuamotus, Society Islands and Uvea (Wallis Island).

properties.label: Bougainville
properties.summary: First French circumnavigation: Tahiti, Samoa, northern Vanuatu, the Great Barrier Reef edge, the Louisiades and the Solomons (Bougainville Island).

properties.label: Bruce
properties.summary: Reached Gondar in 1770 and the Blue Nile springs at Gish Abay, then returned via Sennar and the Nubian desert; his Travels (1790) mapped Abyssinia and the Blue Nile.

properties.label: Cook 1
properties.summary: Observed the Transit of Venus at Tahiti, charted the whole of New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, and passed through Torres Strait.

properties.label: Hearne
properties.summary: First European overland journey to the Arctic coast, at the Coppermine mouth, and first to cross Great Slave Lake.

properties.label: Kerguelen
