properties.summary: Search for Terra Australis from Mauritius that discovered the Kerguelen Islands in the southern Indian Ocean.

properties.label: Cook 2a
properties.summary: First crossing of the Antarctic Circle (17 January 1773) and a long sweep of the high southern latitudes, then Tahiti and Tonga.

properties.label: Cook 2b
properties.summary: Reached 71 10 S, then charted Easter Island, the Marquesas, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Norfolk Island, and returned via South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.

properties.label: Kerguelen II
properties.summary: Second expedition (Roland and Oiseau) revisited Kerguelen and showed the islands barren, ending hopes of a southern continent there.

properties.label: Phipps
properties.summary: Attempt on the North Pole via Spitsbergen, blocked by ice at about 80 48 N near the Seven Islands.

properties.label: Bogle
properties.summary: Warren Hastings' envoy through Bhutan to the Panchen Lama near Shigatse, the first British mission to Tibet.

properties.label: Cook 3a
properties.summary: Third voyage outward leg: Tasmania, New Zealand, the Cook Islands, Tonga, Tubuai, Tahiti, Kiritimati and the first European landfall in Hawaii.

properties.label: Cook NW coast
properties.summary: Charted the Northwest Coast from Oregon to Nootka, Prince William Sound, Cook Inlet and the Aleutians.

properties.label: Cook 3b
properties.summary: Charted the north-west coast of America from Oregon to the Bering Strait, reached Icy Cape at 70 N, and after Cook's death Clerke probed the Arctic again from Kamchatka.

properties.leader: Jean-Francois de Galaup, comte de La Perouse
properties.label: La Perouse
properties.summary: Pacific crossing via Easter Island and Maui to the Alaska coast (Lituya Bay), south to Monterey and across to the Marianas and Manila.

properties.leader: Jean-Francois de Galaup, comte de La Perouse
properties.label: La Perouse 2
properties.summary: Explored the Sea of Japan, the Tartary coast and the strait now named for him, then via Kamchatka, Samoa and Botany Bay to his wreck at Vanikoro.

properties.label: Bligh
properties.summary: Open-boat voyage after the Bounty mutiny, from Tofua through Fiji and the Banks Islands to Timor, sketching coasts along the way.

properties.label: Mackenzie 1789
properties.summary: Descended the Mackenzie River from Great Slave Lake to the Arctic Ocean.

properties.label: Turnor and Fidler
properties.summary: Survey from Cumberland House to Lake Athabasca and Great Slave Lake, fixing positions for the first accurate maps.

properties.label: Malaspina
properties.summary: Spanish scientific expedition's survey of Yakutat Bay, Prince William Sound, Nootka and Monterey.

properties.label: Vancouver
properties.summary: Pacific legs: King George Sound in south-west Australia, Dusky Sound, the Snares, Rapa, Tahiti and Hawaii, before his survey of the North American coast.

properties.label: d'Entrecasteaux
properties.summary: Searching for La Perouse, charted south-east Tasmania, New Caledonia, the Solomons and Louisiades, the south coast of Australia and the north coast of New Guinea.

properties.label: Mackenzie 1793
properties.summary: First recorded crossing of North America north of Mexico, via the Peace and Fraser rivers to the Pacific at Dean Channel.

properties.label: Vancouver
properties.summary: Detailed survey of the Northwest Coast from California to Cook Inlet, including Puget Sound and the Inside Passage.

properties.label: Park (1st)
properties.summary: From Pisania on the Gambia through Kaarta and Ludamar to the Niger at Ségou (21 July 1796), proving it flows east, then back by a more southerly route.

properties.label: Bass and Flinders
properties.summary: Circumnavigated Van Diemen's Land, proving Bass Strait separates Tasmania from the mainland.

properties.label: Hornemann
properties.summary: German in British service who crossed from Cairo via Siwa and Awjila to Murzuk in Fezzan, the first European there in modern times.

properties.label: Lacerda
properties.summary: Portuguese expedition from Tete to the court of the Kazembe south of Lake Mweru, where Lacerda died; his diary mapped the route.

properties.label: Humboldt Orinoco
properties.summary: Proved the Casiquiare links the Orinoco and Amazon basins; first scientific mapping of the upper Orinoco.

properties.label: Baudin
properties.summary: Charted much of the west, south (Terre Napoleon) and Tasmanian coasts, with major natural history and ethnographic collections.

properties.label: Flinders
properties.summary: First circumnavigation of Australia, charting the south coast and the Gulf of Carpentaria and popularising the name Australia.

properties.label: Humboldt Andes
properties.summary: Magdalena, Bogota, Quito and Chimborazo to Lima: founded the science of Andean geography and plant zones.

properties.leader: Pedro João Baptista and Amaro José (pombeiros)
properties.label: Pombeiros crossing
properties.summary: Two Afro-Portuguese trading agents made the first recorded crossing of south-central Africa, from Kasanje in Angola via the Lunda and Kazembe to Tete.

properties.label: Humboldt Mexico
properties.summary: Survey of New Spain from Acapulco to Mexico City, Guanajuato and Veracruz, basis of his Political Essay.

properties.label: Lewis and Clark
properties.summary: Up the Missouri, over the Lemhi and Lolo passes and down the Snake and Columbia to the Pacific.

properties.label: Park (2nd)
properties.summary: Descended the Niger in the boat Joliba from Sansanding past Timbuktu and Gao to the Bussa rapids, where he drowned; the river's lower course remained unknown.

properties.label: Clark Yellowstone
properties.summary: Return by the Yellowstone River, the first European descent of it.

properties.label: GTS south
properties.summary: Lambton's triangulation from the 1802 Madras baseline across the peninsula to Mangalore and down to Cape Comorin fixed south India accurately.

properties.label: Lewis Marias
properties.summary: Return across the Continental Divide by the Blackfoot River and up the Marias.

properties.label: Pike
properties.summary: Up the Arkansas to the Colorado Rockies (Pikes Peak), then taken by Spanish troops through Santa Fe and Chihuahua.

properties.label: Fraser
properties.summary: Descended the Fraser River through its canyons to the Strait of Georgia.

properties.label: Manning
properties.summary: First Englishman to reach Lhasa, where he met the young 9th Dalai Lama.

properties.label: Thompson
properties.summary: Crossed Athabasca Pass and became the first European to travel the whole Columbia to its mouth.

properties.label: Burckhardt Petra
properties.summary: Travelling as Sheikh Ibrahim, he reached Petra, the first European to see it since the Crusades, then crossed Sinai to Cairo.

properties.leader: Gregory Blaxland; William Lawson; William Charles Wentworth
properties.label: Blue Mountains
properties.summary: First recorded European crossing of the Blue Mountains west of Sydney, opening the inland plains.

properties.label: Burckhardt Nubia
properties.summary: Travelled up the Nile through Nubia to near the Third Cataract and on the way back found the sand-buried temple of Abu Simbel.

properties.label: Burckhardt to Shendi
properties.summary: Crossed the Nubian desert to Berber and Shendi near Meroë, then to Taka and Suakin on the Red Sea, describing the Sudanese Nile towns.

properties.label: Burckhardt Mecca
properties.summary: Made the Hajj and gave Europe the first accurate descriptions of Mecca and Medina.

properties.label: Kotzebue
properties.summary: Discovered Kotzebue Sound in Alaska and charted the Ratak chain of the Marshall Islands in detail.

properties.label: Oxley
properties.summary: Traced the Lachlan and Macquarie rivers into the inland marshes, then crossed the Liverpool Plains and the Great Dividing Range to Port Macquarie.

properties.leader: Johann Baptist von Spix, Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius
properties.label: Spix and Martius
properties.summary: Crossed Brazil from Rio to Bahia, Maranhao and Belem, then up the Amazon to its upper reaches.

properties.label: Ross 1818
properties.summary: Re-surveyed Baffin Bay, met the Inughuit of the Thule region, and turned back in Lancaster Sound believing it closed by mountains.

properties.leader: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen; Mikhail Lazarev
properties.label: Bellingshausen
properties.summary: First Russian Antarctic expedition: sighted the Antarctic ice shelf on 28 January 1820 and later Peter I Island and Alexander I Land, also charting Tuamotu islands.

properties.leader: John Franklin; John Richardson; George Back
properties.label: Franklin (Coppermine)
properties.summary: Overland to the Coppermine River mouth and east along the Arctic coast to Point Turnagain; disastrous starvation on the return.

properties.label: Parry
properties.summary: Sailed through Lancaster Sound and Barrow Strait to winter at Melville Island, more than halfway through the Northwest Passage.

properties.label: Sadleir
properties.summary: First European to cross the Arabian peninsula, from the Gulf coast to Medina and Yanbu, chasing Ibrahim Pasha's army.

properties.label: Cailliaud
properties.summary: Accompanied Ismail Pasha's conquest of the Sudan, describing Meroë's pyramids and the Blue Nile up to Fazogli; published as Voyage à Méroé (1826).

properties.label: Moorcroft
properties.summary: Explored Ladakh and Kashmir, then crossed the Hindu Kush to Bukhara; Moorcroft died at Andkhoy.

properties.leader: Hugh Clapperton, Dixon Denham and Walter Oudney
properties.label: Bornu Mission
properties.summary: First Europeans to cross the Sahara from Tripoli to Bornu, reaching Lake Chad (4 Feb 1823) and Kukawa.

properties.label: Clapperton to Sokoto
properties.summary: Clapperton went west through Kano to Sultan Bello's Sokoto, the first European description of the Hausa states and the Sokoto Caliphate.

properties.label: Denham round Lake Chad
properties.summary: Joined a raid into the Mandara mountains and surveyed the western and southern shores of Lake Chad and the lower Logone and Shari.

properties.label: Weddell
properties.summary: Sealer sailed into the sea now named for him, reaching 74 15 S in an unusually open season.

properties.label: Hume and Hovell
properties.summary: Overland from New South Wales to Port Phillip, finding the upper Murray (named the Hume) and good grazing country.

properties.label: Clapperton (2nd)
properties.summary: From Badagry through Yoruba country, across the Niger at Bussa and on to Kano and Sokoto, where Clapperton died in April 1827.

properties.label: Franklin (Mackenzie)
properties.summary: Second Arctic land expedition: down the Mackenzie and west along the Alaskan coast to Return Reef, while Richardson charted east to the Coppermine.

properties.label: Laing
properties.summary: First European known to reach Timbuktu (Aug 1826), via Ghadames, In Salah and the Tanezrouft; he was killed on leaving and his papers were lost.

properties.label: d'Urville
properties.summary: Charted New Zealand's coasts, Tonga, Fiji, the Loyalty Islands, New Britain and northern New Guinea, and found La Perouse's wreck at Vanikoro.

properties.label: Langsdorff
properties.summary: Canoe expedition from Sao Paulo via the Tiete, Pardo and Paraguay to Cuiaba, then down the Arinos, Juruena and Tapajos.

properties.label: Caillié
properties.summary: Disguised as a Muslim, walked from the Rio Nunez via Djenné to Timbuktu (April 1828) and was the first European to return alive, crossing the Sahara to Morocco.

properties.label: Sturt (Darling)
properties.summary: Followed the Macquarie beyond its marshes and found the Darling River.

properties.label: Ross 1829
properties.summary: Steam vessel Victory explored Prince Regent Inlet and the Gulf of Boothia, wintering four times at Felix Harbour on Boothia.

properties.label: Sturt (Murray)
properties.summary: Rowed down the Murrumbidgee and the Murray, past the Darling junction, to Lake Alexandrina, revealing the great inland river system.

properties.label: Biscoe
properties.summary: Third circumnavigation of Antarctica; sighted Enderby Land (1831) and Adelaide Island and the Biscoe Islands off Graham Land (1832).

properties.label: Magnetic Pole (N)
properties.summary: Sledged across Boothia to the north-west coast of King William Island (1830) and reached the North Magnetic Pole on the Boothia coast (1 June 1831).

properties.label: Lander brothers
properties.summary: Followed the lower Niger from Bussa to the delta, proving that Park's river reaches the Gulf of Guinea.

properties.label: Monteiro and Gamitto
properties.summary: Portuguese expedition from Tete through Chewa and Bisa country to the Kazembe; Gamitto's O Muata Cazembe (1854) described the region.

properties.label: Beagle survey
properties.summary: Hydrographic survey of the coasts of Argentina, Tierra del Fuego and Chile, with Darwin's natural history.

properties.label: Burnes
properties.summary: Travels into Bokhara: from Lahore over the Hindu Kush to Bukhara and back through Merv and Persia.

properties.label: Santa Cruz river
properties.summary: Boat party up the Santa Cruz River to within sight of the Andes.

properties.label: Mitchell
properties.summary: Australia Felix expedition: the Lachlan and Murray, then south-west across western Victoria to the Grampians, Glenelg and Portland Bay.

properties.label: d'Urville (Antarctic)
properties.summary: Charted Joinville Island and Louis Philippe Land (1838) and discovered Adelie Land, landing near Point Geologie (January 1840).

properties.label: Wilkes
properties.summary: United States Exploring Expedition sailed west along some 2,400 km of the East Antarctic coast, establishing that Antarctica is a continent.

properties.label: Eyre
properties.summary: First east to west crossing along the Great Australian Bight (Nullarbor coast) from Fowlers Bay to Albany, after probing Lake Torrens to Mount Hopeless.

properties.label: Ross Sea
properties.summary: Broke through the pack into the Ross Sea, charting Victoria Land, Ross Island volcanoes and the Great Ice Barrier, and reached 78 10 S in 1842.

properties.label: Great Arc
properties.summary: The Great Arc meridian survey from Cape Comorin to the Himalayan foothills near Mussoorie, the spine of the survey of India.

properties.label: Fremont 1842
properties.summary: Surveyed the Oregon Trail to South Pass and the Wind River Range.

properties.label: Fremont 1843
properties.summary: Great loop to Oregon, across the Great Basin (which he named), over the Sierra in winter and back via Utah.

properties.label: Huc and Gabet
properties.summary: Lazarist missionaries crossed Mongolia, the Ordos and Kokonor to Lhasa, then were escorted out to Sichuan.

properties.label: Leichhardt
properties.summary: Overland from the Darling Downs to Port Essington, opening the Dawson, Burdekin, Mitchell and Roper river country and the southern Gulf of Carpentaria.

properties.label: Sturt (Centre)
properties.summary: Central Australian expedition via the Darling and Depot Glen into the Strzelecki and Sturt Stony deserts, reaching the edge of the Simpson Desert.

properties.label: Franklin (lost)
properties.summary: Last Franklin expedition: circled Cornwallis Island, wintered at Beechey Island and was beset off King William Island, where all 129 men died.

properties.label: Richardson (1st)
properties.summary: British anti-slavery traveller who visited Ghadames, Ghat and Murzuk, describing the central Saharan caravan towns.

properties.label: Brunner
properties.summary: The Great Journey: 550 days down the Buller River and the West Coast to near Paringa, finding the Grey valley and the Brunner coalfield.

properties.label: Kennedy
properties.summary: Attempted to traverse Cape York Peninsula from Rockingham Bay; most of the party died.

properties.label: Rebmann to Kilimanjaro
properties.summary: German missionary who saw snow on Kilimanjaro in May 1848, a report doubted in London but later confirmed.

properties.label: Knoblecher on the White Nile
properties.summary: Slovene missionary who ascended the White Nile to Gondokoro, following the Egyptian river expeditions of 1839 to 1842.

properties.label: Krapf to Kitui
properties.summary: Walked from Rabai to Kitui in Ukambani and was the first European to see Mount Kenya (Dec 1849).

properties.leader: David Livingstone (with William Cotton Oswell and Mungo Murray)
properties.label: Livingstone to Ngami
properties.summary: Crossed the Kalahari from Kolobeng to Lake Ngami.

properties.leader: Heinrich Barth, James Richardson and Adolf Overweg
properties.label: Barth: Tripoli to Kukawa
properties.summary: British-sponsored mission across the Sahara via Ghat and Aïr to Agadez (Oct 1850), Kano and Bornu.

properties.label: McClure
properties.summary: Entered from Bering Strait, found Prince of Wales Strait and was trapped at Mercy Bay on Banks Island; completed the first transit of the passage partly on foot.

properties.label: Barth to Adamawa
properties.summary: First European in Adamawa, reaching the upper Benue near Yola.

properties.leader: David Livingstone and William Cotton Oswell
properties.label: Livingstone to the Zambezi
properties.summary: Reached the upper Zambezi at Sesheke in Kololo country (Aug 1851), revealing a great river in the heart of the continent.

properties.label: Overweg on Lake Chad
properties.summary: Sailed the boat carried across the Sahara around Lake Chad and its Buduma islands, the first European navigation of the lake.

properties.label: Barth: Kukawa to Timbuktu
properties.summary: Visited Bagirmi (1852), then went west through Sokoto and across the Niger at Say to Timbuktu (Sept 1853).

properties.label: Burton Mecca
properties.summary: Disguised as a pilgrim, went from Yanbu to Medina and by the eastern caravan road to Mecca.

properties.label: Linyanti to Luanda
properties.summary: Went up the Barotse valley and across the Kasai watershed to Luanda (May 1854), with 27 Kololo companions.

properties.label: Vogel
properties.summary: Sent to reinforce Barth; explored Bauchi and the Benue, then was killed entering Wadai in 1856.

properties.label: Barth: Timbuktu to Tripoli
properties.summary: Mapped the Niger bend between Timbuktu and Say, passing Gao, then returned to Tripoli via Bornu and Bilma (Sept 1855).

properties.label: Burton to Harar
properties.summary: Disguised as an Arab merchant, Burton was the first European to enter Harar (3 Jan 1855), returning via Berbera.

properties.label: Livingstone to Quelimane
properties.summary: Followed the Zambezi from Linyanti past Victoria Falls (Nov 1855) to Tete and Quelimane, completing the first recorded European coast-to-coast crossing of southern Africa.

properties.label: Gregory
properties.summary: North Australian Expedition from the Victoria River to Sturt Creek and Lake Gregory, then east across the Gulf country to Brisbane.

properties.leader: Andrew Waugh and Survey of India computers
properties.label: Himalayan peaks
properties.summary: Peaks of the Himalaya, including Peak XV (Everest) and Kangchenjunga, fixed from stations on the plains, since Nepal and Tibet were closed.

properties.leader: Richard Francis Burton and John Hanning Speke
properties.label: Burton and Speke
properties.summary: Followed the Arab caravan route from the coast via Kazeh (Tabora) to Ujiji, the first Europeans to see Lake Tanganyika (Feb 1858).

properties.leader: David Livingstone (Zambezi Expedition, with John Kirk)
properties.label: Zambezi Expedition
properties.summary: Steamed up the Zambezi to the Cahora Bassa rapids and up the Shire to Lake Chilwa and Lake Malawi, then boated up the lake's west shore.

properties.label: Mouhot
properties.summary: Popularised Angkor in Europe and travelled from Bangkok via Korat to Luang Prabang, where he died.

properties.label: Speke to Lake Victoria
properties.summary: Detoured north from Kazeh and reached Lake Victoria at Mwanza (30 July or 3 Aug 1858), guessing it was the Nile's source.

properties.label: Duveyrier
properties.summary: Young Frenchman who lived among the Kel Ajjer Tuareg, visiting El Golea, Ghadames and Ghat; Les Touareg du Nord (1864) was the first study of them.

properties.leader: Robert O'Hara Burke; William John Wills
properties.label: Burke and Wills
properties.summary: First south to north crossing of Australia from Melbourne via Menindee and Cooper Creek to the tidal Flinders River near the Gulf of Carpentaria.

properties.leader: John Hanning Speke and James Augustus Grant
properties.label: Speke and Grant
properties.summary: Via Karagwe and Buganda to Ripon Falls, where the Nile leaves Lake Victoria (28 July 1862), then down through Bunyoro to Gondokoro and Khartoum.

properties.label: Bakers on the Atbara
properties.summary: Spent a year exploring the Atbara, Setit, Rahad and Dinder, the Ethiopian tributaries that bring the Nile flood.

properties.label: Stuart
properties.summary: First successful south to north crossing through the centre, from Chambers Creek to Chambers Bay near Darwin; the route of the Overland Telegraph.

properties.label: Bakers to Lake Albert
properties.summary: From Gondokoro through Latuka and Bunyoro to Lake Albert (14 March 1864) and Murchison Falls, adding the second great Nile lake.

properties.label: Palgrave
properties.summary: Crossed northern and central Arabia from Ma'an via Jawf, Hail and Riyadh to Hofuf and the Gulf.

properties.label: Tinne Bahr el Ghazal
properties.summary: Dutch traveller's expedition up the Bahr el Ghazal to Meshra er-Rek and overland toward the Azande country.

properties.label: Vambery
properties.summary: Disguised as a dervish, crossed the Turkmen desert to Khiva, Bukhara and Samarkand and returned via Herat.

properties.label: Kashmir survey
properties.summary: Montgomerie's Kashmir and Karakoram triangulation (1855-1864) mapped the western Himalaya and fixed K2.

properties.label: Nain Singh
properties.summary: Counting paces with a rosary, the pundit fixed Lhasa's position and surveyed the Tsangpo trade route from Nepal to Lhasa and west to Manasarovar.

properties.label: Rohlfs: Tripoli to Lagos
properties.summary: First European crossing from the Mediterranean to the Gulf of Guinea, via Bornu, Bauchi and the Benue confluence to Lagos.

properties.leader: Ernest Doudart de Lagree and Francis Garnier
properties.label: Mekong Expedition
properties.summary: French Mekong Commission traced the river from Cambodia through Laos to Yunnan, showing it was unnavigable, then descended the Yangtze to Shanghai.

properties.label: Livingstone's last journey
properties.summary: From the Rovuma round Lake Malawi to Lakes Mweru and Bangweulu and the Lualaba at Nyangwe, dying at Chitambo's village in 1873.

properties.leader: Nain Singh, Mani Singh and Kalian Singh (Pundits)
properties.label: Thok Jalung
properties.summary: Reached the Thok Jalung goldfields of western Tibet and mapped the upper Sutlej and Gartok.

properties.label: Przhevalsky Ussuri
properties.summary: Explored the Ussuri basin, Lake Khanka and the Pacific coast of the newly annexed Primorye.

properties.label: Baker in Equatoria
properties.summary: As governor of Equatoria for the Khedive, Baker extended Egyptian rule south from Gondokoro to Bunyoro (Masindi).

properties.label: Nachtigal to Tibesti
properties.summary: First European to enter the Tibesti mountains, reaching Bardai.

properties.label: Powell
properties.summary: First descent of the Green and Colorado rivers through the Grand Canyon, filling the last large blank in the US map.

properties.label: Schweinfurth
properties.summary: Botanist who went via the Bahr el Ghazal through Bongo and Azande country to the Mangbetu and found the Uele flowing west, a river of the Congo basin.

properties.label: Nachtigal across the Sudan
properties.summary: From Bornu to Kanem, Borku, Bagirmi, Wadai, Darfur and Kordofan to Khartoum, the first European to traverse the eastern Sudan belt.

properties.label: Przhevalsky 1
properties.summary: Crossed the Gobi to Peking, explored the Ordos and Alashan, the Kokonor and Tsaidam, and reached the upper Yangtze in northern Tibet.

properties.label: Stanley finds Livingstone
properties.summary: Marched from the coast via Tabora to Ujiji, found Livingstone (10 Nov 1871), and with him explored the north end of Lake Tanganyika.

properties.label: Tegetthoff
properties.summary: Austro-Hungarian Tegetthoff drifted in pack ice to discover Franz Josef Land; Payer sledged north to Cape Fligely at 81 50 N.

properties.label: Cameron
properties.summary: First European to cross equatorial Africa from sea to sea, surveying Lake Tanganyika and its Lukuga outlet and following the Congo-Zambezi watershed to Benguela.

properties.label: Rohlfs Libyan Desert
properties.summary: Scientific expedition from Dakhla into the Great Sand Sea, turning north to Siwa.

properties.label: Warburton
properties.summary: First crossing of the Great Sandy Desert by camel, from Alice Springs to the Oakover River and Roebourne.

properties.label: Forrest
properties.summary: West to east crossing from Geraldton through the Gibson Desert margin to the Overland Telegraph Line.

properties.label: Nain Singh 2
properties.summary: Crossed the northern Changtang lakes from Ladakh to Lhasa, then south through Tawang to Assam, revealing a vast unknown plateau.

properties.label: Stanley across Africa
properties.sponsor: UK and USA (Daily Telegraph, New York Herald)
properties.summary: Circumnavigated Lakes Victoria and Tanganyika, then followed the Lualaba from Nyangwe to the Atlantic, proving it was the Congo (Boma, 9 Aug 1877).

properties.leader: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza (with Noël Ballay and Alfred Marche)
properties.label: Brazza on the Ogooué
properties.summary: Ascended the Ogooué to its headwaters and crossed to the Alima, a Congo tributary.

properties.label: Giles
properties.summary: Camel crossing of the Great Victoria Desert from South Australia via Queen Victoria Spring to Perth.

properties.label: Nares
properties.summary: British Arctic Expedition pushed ships up Smith Sound and Kennedy and Robeson channels; Markham's sledge party reached 83 20 N.

properties.label: Fly River
properties.sponsor: Italy (private; New South Wales steam launch)
properties.summary: Steamed hundreds of kilometres up the Fly River aboard the Neva, the deepest European penetration of New Guinea at the time.

properties.label: Doughty
properties.summary: Travels in Arabia Deserta: Mada'in Salih, Tayma, Hail, Khaybar and Unaizah, the classic account of the Najd Bedouin.

properties.label: Emin in Buganda
properties.summary: As Gordon's officer, made missions from Lado to Buganda and Bunyoro, describing their courts and natural history.

properties.label: Moreno 1876
properties.summary: Up the Rio Negro and Limay to Lake Nahuel Huapi.

properties.label: Potanin Mongolia
properties.summary: Surveyed north-western Mongolia from Zaysan to Kobdo, Hami and Uliastai.

properties.label: Przhevalsky Lop Nur
properties.summary: Reached Lop Nur and the Altyn-Tagh from Kulja via the Yulduz and the lower Tarim.

properties.label: Capelo and Ivens (1st)
properties.summary: Explored the upper Kwango and the Yaka country between Bié and Luanda.

properties.label: Moreno 1877
properties.summary: Up the Santa Cruz River to the lake he named Lago Argentino, and onward to Lago Viedma.

properties.label: Serpa Pinto
properties.summary: Crossed from Benguela via Bié and the upper Zambezi to Victoria Falls and Pretoria.

properties.leader: Kishen Singh (Krishna Singh Rawat, Pundit A-K)
properties.label: Kishen Singh
properties.summary: Four-year pundit journey from Darjeeling through Lhasa to the Tsaidam and Dunhuang, returning across the Mekong, Salween and Irrawaddy headwaters.

properties.label: Vega
properties.summary: First complete transit of the Northeast Passage, rounding Cape Chelyuskin and wintering on the Chukchi coast before passing Bering Strait.

properties.label: Rohlfs to Kufra
properties.summary: First European to reach the Kufra oases in the Libyan desert (1879).

properties.label: Junker
properties.summary: Explored the Uele and Ubangi watershed among the Azande and Mangbetu, then escaped Mahdist Sudan via Bunyoro, Buganda and Zanzibar.

properties.label: Lenz to Timbuktu
properties.summary: First trans-Saharan expedition from Morocco via Tindouf and Taoudenni to Timbuktu and on to Senegal.

properties.label: Przhevalsky 3
properties.summary: Via Hami and the Tsaidam to within about 260 km of Lhasa before being turned back, then explored the upper Yellow River.

properties.label: Thomson to the lakes
properties.summary: Took over when Johnston died and reached Lakes Nyasa and Tanganyika, the Lukuga outlet and Lake Rukwa.

properties.label: Brazza to Stanley Pool
properties.summary: Crossed from Franceville to the Batéké kingdom, signed the Makoko treaty and founded the post at Stanley Pool that became Brazzaville.

properties.label: Flatters
properties.summary: French railway survey toward the Ahaggar, annihilated by Kel Ahaggar Tuareg at Bir el-Gharama (Feb 1881).

properties.label: Wissmann across Africa
properties.summary: Crossed Africa from Luanda via the Kasai and Lulua to Nyangwe and Tabora to the east coast.

properties.leader: Nikolay Przhevalsky, Vsevolod Roborovsky and Pyotr Kozlov
properties.label: Przhevalsky 4
properties.summary: Reached the sources of the Yellow River, then went west along the Kunlun to Khotan and north to Lake Issyk-Kul.

properties.label: Thomson through Masai land
properties.summary: First European through Maasai country from the coast to Lake Victoria, via Naivasha, Baringo and Mount Elgon.

properties.label: Angola to Mozambique
properties.summary: Crossed from Moçâmedes via the upper Zambezi and Katanga (Msiri's Garanganja) to Tete and Quelimane, backing Portugal's pink-map claim.

properties.label: Potanin Gansu
properties.summary: From Peking across the Ordos to Lanzhou and Xining, south over the eastern Tibetan plateau to Songpan and back, wintering at Kumbum.

properties.label: Binger
properties.summary: From the Niger via Sikasso, Kong, Bobo-Dioulasso and Ouagadougou to Salaga and the Ivory Coast, proving the 'Mountains of Kong' did not exist.

properties.label: Pavie
properties.summary: Pavie Mission surveyed Laos and the Tai uplands from Luang Prabang across to Hanoi, laying the basis for French Indochina's maps.

properties.leader: Henry Morton Stanley (Emin Pasha Relief Expedition)
properties.label: Emin Pasha Relief
properties.sponsor: Britain (relief committee) and Congo Free State
properties.summary: Up the Congo and Aruwimi and through the Ituri forest to Lake Albert, then south past the Ruwenzori and Lake Edward to the east coast.

properties.leader: Sámuel Teleki and Ludwig von Höhnel
properties.label: Teleki and Höhnel
properties.summary: Via Kilimanjaro and Mount Kenya to Lake Rudolf (Turkana) and Lake Stefanie, the last large East African lakes unknown to Europe.

properties.label: Younghusband
properties.summary: Peking to India across the Gobi and the Tarim towns, then over the Mustagh Pass in the Karakoram to Kashmir.

properties.label: Nansen (Greenland)
properties.summary: First crossing of the Greenland ice sheet, from Umivik on the east coast to Ameralik fjord and Godthab.

properties.label: Pevtsov
properties.summary: Led Przhevalsky's last expedition after his death, surveying the Kunlun front, Niya, Lop Nur and the Turfan depression.

properties.label: Emin's last expedition
properties.summary: German expedition from the coast via Bukoba and the Lake Albert region into the Ituri, ending with Emin's murder near Kinena (Oct 1892).

properties.label: Monteil
properties.summary: French officer who marched from Ségou to Say, Sokoto, Kano and Bornu, then crossed the Sahara to Tripoli.

properties.label: Peary (Greenland)
properties.summary: Crossed the north Greenland ice sheet to Independence Fjord (Navy Cliff), indicating Greenland's northern limit.

properties.label: Fram
properties.summary: Fram drifted with the pack ice across the Arctic Ocean from the New Siberian Islands to north of Spitsbergen, proving there was no polar continent.

properties.label: Hedin Taklamakan
properties.summary: Nearly died crossing the Taklamakan, then found the buried cities of Dandan-Uiliq and crossed to Lop Nur, Tsaidam and Peking.

properties.label: Kingsley on the Ogooué
properties.summary: Canoed up the Ogooué beyond Lambaréné and crossed Fang country to the Rembwe, describing the region in Travels in West Africa (1897).

properties.label: Farthest North
properties.summary: Left the Fram to reach a Farthest North of 86 13.6 N, then retreated to winter on Franz Josef Land before meeting Jackson at Cape Flora.

properties.label: Marchand to Fashoda
properties.summary: Crossed from the Loango coast via the Ubangi and Bahr el Ghazal to Fashoda on the White Nile (July 1898), then out through Ethiopia to Djibouti.

properties.label: Southern Cross
properties.summary: First wintering on the Antarctic mainland at Cape Adare, and first landing and sledge journey on the Great Ice Barrier (78 50 S).

properties.label: Belgica
properties.summary: Charted the Gerlache Strait and then made the first wintering south of the Antarctic Circle, beset in the Bellingshausen Sea.

properties.label: Foureau-Lamy
properties.summary: First French military crossing of the Sahara, from Ouargla via the Aïr and Zinder to Lake Chad (Kousseri, 1900); Foureau continued down the Shari, Ubangi and Congo to the Atlantic.

properties.label: Sverdrup
properties.summary: Second Fram expedition: from Jones Sound, sledge parties discovered and mapped Axel Heiberg, Ellef Ringnes and Amund Ringnes islands.

properties.label: Hedin Loulan
properties.summary: Mapped the Tarim by boat, discovered the ruins of Loulan and crossed the Changtang towards Lhasa before being turned back.

properties.label: Kozlov Kham
properties.summary: Mongolia-Kham expedition through the Gobi Altai and Tsaidam into eastern Tibet.

properties.label: Stein 1
properties.summary: Archaeological survey of the southern Tarim: Khotan, Dandan-Uiliq and Niya.

properties.leader: Robert Falcon Scott; Ernest Shackleton; Edward Wilson
properties.label: Discovery
properties.summary: Discovery expedition: southern sledge journey to 82 17 S along the Barrier, and the 1903 western journey up the Ferrar Glacier onto the polar plateau.

properties.label: Gjoa
properties.summary: First complete navigation of the Northwest Passage by a single ship, wintering at Gjoa Haven on King William Island.

properties.label: Fawcett 1906
properties.summary: Boundary survey of the Bolivia-Brazil-Peru frontier in the Acre and Abuna region.

properties.label: Hedin Transhimalaya
properties.summary: Crossed the Transhimalaya repeatedly, visited Shigatse and traced the sources of the Brahmaputra, Indus and Sutlej.

properties.label: Stein 2
properties.summary: Second expedition: Miran, the Lop desert, the Dunhuang library cave and the Gansu Nan Shan, with Survey of India mapping.

properties.label: Kozlov Khara-Khoto
properties.summary: Discovered the Tangut city of Khara-Khoto in the Gobi and explored Amdo.

properties.label: Rondon
properties.summary: Telegraph-line surveys across Mato Grosso and Rondonia from Cuiaba to the Madeira.

properties.leader: Edgeworth David; Douglas Mawson; Alistair Mackay
properties.label: Magnetic Pole
properties.summary: Northern Party man-hauled up the Victoria Land coast and across the plateau to the South Magnetic Pole.

properties.label: Nimrod
properties.summary: Southern journey pioneered the Beardmore Glacier route and reached 88 23 S, 180 km from the South Pole.

properties.label: Peary (Pole)
properties.summary: Claimed sledge journey from Cape Columbia to the North Pole (April 1909).

properties.label: Amundsen (Pole)
properties.summary: First to reach the South Pole (14 December 1911) from the Bay of Whales via the Axel Heiberg Glacier, revealing the Queen Maud Mountains.

properties.label: Deutschland
properties.summary: Penetrated deepest into the Weddell Sea, discovering the Luitpold Coast and the Filchner Ice Shelf, then drifted north in the pack.

properties.label: Aurora
properties.summary: Australasian Antarctic Expedition charted the coast from Commonwealth Bay to Queen Mary Land and set up a station on Macquarie Island.

properties.label: Terra Nova
properties.summary: Reached the South Pole on 17 January 1912 via the Beardmore Glacier, 33 days after Amundsen; all five died on the return.

properties.leader: Douglas Mawson; Belgrave Ninnis; Xavier Mertz
properties.label: Far Eastern Party
properties.summary: Sledged east across the Mertz and Ninnis glaciers into George V Land; Mawson alone survived the return.

properties.label: Koch-Wegener
properties.summary: Danish expedition crossed the Greenland ice sheet at its widest, from Dronning Louise Land to the Upernavik district, with glaciological measurements.

properties.label: River of Doubt
properties.sponsor: Brazil / American Museum of Natural History
properties.summary: First descent of the River of Doubt (Rio Roosevelt), a 1,000 km tributary of the Madeira.

properties.label: Vilkitsky
properties.summary: Icebreakers Taymyr and Vaygach discovered Severnaya Zemlya (1913) and made the first east to west transit of the Northeast Passage (1914 to 1915).

properties.label: Endurance
properties.summary: Endurance was beset and crushed in the Weddell Sea; the crew drifted on the ice to Elephant Island and Shackleton sailed the James Caird to South Georgia.

properties.label: Maud
properties.summary: Maud expedition along the Northeast Passage, wintering off Cape Chelyuskin and Ayon Island, with oceanographic work on the Siberian shelf.

properties.leader: Charles Howard-Bury, George Mallory, Guy Bullock, Oliver Wheeler
properties.label: Everest 1921
properties.summary: First reconnaissance of Everest from Tibet, mapping its northern approaches and finding the route to the North Col.

properties.label: Fifth Thule
properties.summary: Dog-sledge journey from Hudson Bay to Nome, recording Inuit communities across Arctic North America.

properties.label: Citroën Sahara crossing
properties.summary: First motor crossing of the Sahara, by Citroën half-tracks from Touggourt to Timbuktu.

properties.label: Hassanein
properties.summary: Egyptian diplomat who rediscovered the lost oases of Arkenu and Uweinat on a camel journey from Sollum to Darfur.

properties.leader: Georges-Marie Haardt and Louis Audouin-Dubreuil (Croisière noire)
properties.label: Croisière noire
properties.summary: Citroën half-track expedition from Colomb-Béchar across the Sahara and the Congo basin to Lake Victoria, filmed and widely publicised.

properties.label: Hamilton Rice
properties.summary: Up the Rio Negro, Rio Branco and Uraricoera toward the Parima, using the first aircraft and shortwave radio in Amazon exploration.

properties.label: Kingdon-Ward
properties.summary: Explored the Tsangpo Gorges round Namcha Barwa, closing most of the gap in the Brahmaputra's course.

properties.label: Fawcett 1925
properties.summary: Final expedition from Cuiaba into the upper Xingu in search of 'Z'; the party vanished.

properties.leader: Roald Amundsen; Lincoln Ellsworth; Umberto Nobile
properties.label: Norge
properties.summary: Airship Norge flew from Spitsbergen over the North Pole to Alaska, showing no land in that sector of the central Arctic.

properties.label: Byrd (N)
properties.summary: Claimed flight from Spitsbergen to the North Pole and back in May 1926.

properties.label: Byrd (S)
properties.summary: First flight over the South Pole (28 to 29 November 1929) from Little America, with aerial survey of the Queen Maud Mountains.

properties.label: Stark Alamut
properties.summary: Mapped the valley of the Assassins' castle of Alamut and travelled in Luristan (The Valleys of the Assassins).

properties.label: Bertram Thomas
properties.summary: First recorded crossing of the Rub' al Khali, from Salalah to Doha.

properties.label: Severnaya Zemlya
properties.summary: Sledge surveys from Domashny Island mapped Severnaya Zemlya and showed it was an archipelago.

properties.label: Wegener
properties.summary: German Greenland Expedition set up the inland station Eismitte; Wegener died on the return in November 1930.

properties.leader: László Almásy (with Robert Clayton East Clayton, Patrick Clayton, H. W. G. J. Penderel)
properties.label: Almásy and the Gilf Kebir
properties.summary: Car and aircraft search for Zerzura that mapped the Gilf Kebir's wadis and in 1933 found the rock paintings of Wadi Sura (Cave of Swimmers).

properties.label: Bagnold
properties.summary: Model T Ford expedition through the Gilf Kebir, Uweinat, Sarra, Tekro and Erdi, mapping the eastern Sahara by car.

properties.label: Philby
properties.summary: Crossed the Empty Quarter from Hofuf via Jabrin and Shanna westwards to Sulaiyil, finding the Wabar craters on the way.

properties.leader: Mick Leahy; Dan Leahy; Jim Taylor
properties.label: Highlands
properties.sponsor: Australia (Territory of New Guinea; gold prospecting)
properties.summary: Following reconnaissance flights, walked into the densely populated Wahgi Valley and Mount Hagen area of the New Guinea Highlands.

properties.label: BGLE
properties.summary: British Graham Land Expedition surveyed the west coast of Graham Land and found George VI Sound, showing Graham Land to be a peninsula.

properties.label: Polar Star
properties.summary: First trans-Antarctic flight, from Dundee Island across the unknown interior of West Antarctica to near Little America.

properties.label: Freya Stark
properties.summary: Travelled inland from Mukalla up the Wadi Do'an to Shibam, Seiyun and Tarim in the Hadhramaut (The Southern Gates of Arabia).

properties.leader: Richard H. Cruzen; Richard E. Byrd
properties.label: Highjump
properties.summary: Large US Navy operation whose aircraft flew to the Pole from Little America and photographed the Marie Byrd Land and Ellsworth Land coasts.

properties.label: Thesiger 1
properties.summary: First crossing of the eastern Rub' al Khali from Mughshin to the Liwa oasis, returning through Oman.

properties.leader: David Bunger; Western Group, Operation Highjump
properties.label: Highjump W
properties.summary: Western Group seaplanes photographed the East Antarctic coast, including the ice-free Bunger Hills.

properties.label: Thesiger 2
properties.summary: Second crossing of the Empty Quarter, from the Hadhramaut to Sulaiyil and on across the sands to Abu Dhabi.

properties.label: Trans-Antarctic
properties.summary: First overland crossing of Antarctica by tractor, from Shackleton Base on the Weddell Sea via the South Pole to Scott Base.

properties.label: Hillary
properties.summary: New Zealand support party laid depots up the Skelton Glacier and drove modified farm tractors to the South Pole.
